title.zh: 卷十九 志第九 禮上
title.raw: 卷十九 志第九 禮上 Volume 19 Treatises 9: Rites Part One

sentences.zh: 禮志上

translations.literal: Rites Monograph, Upper Section (chapter heading).
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites, Part One

sentences.zh: 夫人含天地陰陽之靈，有哀樂喜怒之情。

translations.literal: Man embodies the numinous powers of heaven and earth, yin and yang, and possesses the emotions of grief, joy, anger, and delight.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings partake of the vital forces of heaven and earth, of yin and yang, and they feel sorrow and joy, anger and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 乃聖垂範，以為民極，節其驕淫，以防其暴亂；

translations.literal: Thereupon the sages handed down models, to serve as the ultimate standard for the people; they restrained arrogance and dissipation, and guarded against violence and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: The sages therefore set the pattern for the world, giving the people a polestar by which to live; they curbed wanton pride and excess and checked cruelty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 崇高天地，虔敬鬼神，列尊卑之序，成夫婦之義，然後為國為家，可得而治也。

translations.literal: they exalted heaven and earth, were reverent toward ghosts and spirits, arrayed the order of noble and base, completed the meaning of husband and wife, and only thereafter could there be governing of state and household.
translations.idiomatic: They honored heaven and earth, showed devotion to the spirits, set out who ranks above whom, and secured the moral bond of marriage—only then could a country and a family be ruled in good order.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「一日克己復禮，天下歸仁。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: “In a single day restrain the self and return to ritual, and all under heaven will turn to benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary records: “Master yourself for one day and come back to ritual, and the world will settle into humaneness.”

sentences.zh: 」若乃太一初分，燧人鑽火，志有暢於恭儉，情不由乎玉帛，而酌玄流於春澗之右，焚封豕于秋林之外，亦無得而闕焉。

translations.literal: ” As for when the Grand Unity first divided and Suiren drilled fire, aspirations found release in reverence and frugality, feelings did not depend on jade and silk, yet they poured dark waters on the right bank of spring streams and burned the great boar beyond the autumn woods—nothing in this may be called deficient either.
translations.idiomatic: ” Consider the age when the cosmos first divided and Suiren kindled fire: people’s aims still ran to reverence and thrift, and their hearts did not turn on gifts of jade and silk; they might ladle black water beside a spring torrent or burn a great boar beyond autumn woods—none of that can be dismissed as falling short.

sentences.zh: 軒頊依神，唐虞稽古，逮乎隆周，其文大備。

translations.literal: Xuanyuan and Zhuanxu relied on the spirits; Tang and Yu examined antiquity; down to flourishing Zhou, its pattern was greatly complete.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor and Zhuanxu, who leaned on the divine, through Tang and Yu, who looked back to antiquity, on to high Zhou—by then the cultural forms of ritual were largely in place.

sentences.zh: 或垂百官之範，置不刊之法；

translations.literal: Some handed down models for the hundred offices and set up unalterable laws;
translations.idiomatic: Some issued standards for every office and framed laws meant to endure;

sentences.zh: 或禮經三百，威儀三千，皆所以弘宣天意，雕刻人理。

translations.literal: some had three hundred ritual canons and three thousand rules of deportment—all were means to magnify heaven’s intent and carve human principle.
translations.idiomatic: others codified three hundred ritual texts and three thousand points of ceremony—all to broadcast heaven’s will and give shape to human moral order.

sentences.zh: 叔代澆訛，王風陵謝，事睽光國，禮亦愆家。

translations.literal: In later ages decay and error prevailed, royal influence withered, affairs estranged the glorious state, and ritual faulted within households.
translations.idiomatic: In decadent times morals rotted, royal virtue faded, public life lost its brilliance, and even family ritual slipped into error.

sentences.zh: 趙簡子問太叔以揖讓周旋之禮，對曰：「蓋所謂儀而非禮也。

translations.literal: Zhao Jianzi asked Grand Uncle about the rites of bowing, yielding, and turning in ceremony; he replied: “What is spoken of is observance, not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jianzi questioned Grand Uncle about the etiquette of bows, yielding, and circling in dance; the answer was: “That is what people call outward form, not the inward substance of ritual.

sentences.zh: 」天經地義之道，自茲尤缺。

translations.literal: ” The way of heaven’s warp and earth’s right principle from this grew especially wanting.
translations.idiomatic: ” From that moment the great norms that bind heaven and earth were more gravely incomplete than ever.

sentences.zh: 哀公十一年，孔子自衛反魯，跡三代之典，垂百王之訓，時無明後，道噎不行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Duke Ai, Confucius returned from Wei to Lu, traced the canons of the three dynasties, and handed down instruction for a hundred kings; there was no enlightened successor in his time, and the Way was choked and did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Ai’s eleventh year Confucius came home from Wei to Lu, recovered the statutes of the three ages, and left a teaching for kings yet unborn; no worthy ruler appeared in his day, and the Way was stifled before it could flourish.

sentences.zh: 若夫情尚分流，堤防之仁是棄；

translations.literal: If inclinations favor divergent currents, the dike that is benevolence is abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: When people chase every private inclination, the embankment of humaneness is thrown away;

sentences.zh: 澆訛異術，洙泗之風斯泯。

translations.literal: when decadence and heterodox methods prevail, the wind of Zhu and Si is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: when shallow custom and wrongheaded practice spread, the moral air of the Zhu and Si stream is lost.

sentences.zh: 是以漢文罷再期之喪，中興為一郊之祭，隨時之義，不其然歟！

translations.literal: Hence Emperor Wen of Han abolished the twenty-seven-month mourning; the restored Han made the suburban sacrifice a single rite—the meaning of adapting to the times—is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: That is why Han Wendi did away with the twenty-seven-month funeral, and why the restored Han trimmed the suburban cult to a single round—rites shift with the age, and so they should.

sentences.zh: 而西京元鼎之辰，中興永平之日，疏璧流而延冠帶，啟儒門而引諸生，兩京之盛，於斯為美。

translations.literal: Yet in the Yuanding year of Western Chang’an and the Yongping day of the restored dynasty, hanging disks shone forth and drew in the cap-and-sash, Confucian gates opened and drew in the scholars—both capitals at their height were most splendid in this.
translations.idiomatic: Still, at Western Han’s Yuanding era and Eastern Han’s Yongping reign, jade pendants glittered at court and men of rank crowded in; academy doors swung wide and students flocked—never were the two capitals grander than in those moments.

sentences.zh: 及山魚登俎，澤豕睽經，禮樂恆委，浮華相尚，而郊禋之制，綱紀或存。

translations.literal: When mountain fish ascended the stand and marsh boar departed from the canon, ritual and music lay constantly neglected, vain display was mutually admired, yet the pattern of suburban sacrifice sometimes still endured.
translations.idiomatic: Later, coarse fare stood on the altar while the classical rules for offerings were cast aside; ritual and music were left in the dust and empty show became the fashion, yet the shell of suburban worship sometimes survived.

sentences.zh: 魏氏光宅，憲章斯美。

translations.literal: The Wei, dwelling in splendor, took its constitution from this excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei dynasty, rising in full majesty, claimed this legacy as its model.

sentences.zh: 王肅、高堂隆之徒，博通前載，三千條之禮，十七篇之學，各以舊文增損當世，豈所謂致君於堯舜之道焉。

translations.literal: Men such as Wang Su and Gao Tanglong, broadly versed in past records, with the ritual of three thousand articles and the learning of seventeen pieces, each expanded and trimmed the age using old texts—can this be called the way to bring a ruler to the level of Yao and Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Scholars like Wang Su and Gao Tanglong, steeped in earlier literature, reworked the three thousand ritual items and the seventeen canonical chapters to fit their own day—hardly a recipe, one might say, for making a monarch the peer of Yao or Shun.

sentences.zh: 世屬雕牆，時逢秕政，周因之典，務多違俗，而遺編殘冊，猶有可觀者也。

translations.literal: Generations belonged to carved walls, times met with rotten government; Zhou’s inherited canons strove often against custom, yet surviving patches of compilation still had something worth seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Their age wallowed in ornament while government rotted; Zhou’s received statutes often collided with popular habit, but even the tattered books that survived still repay reading.

sentences.zh: 景初元年，營洛陽南委粟山以為圓丘，祀之日以始祖帝舜配，房俎生魚，陶樽玄酒，非搢紳為之綱紀，其孰能興於此者哉！

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu, they built on Mount Weisu south of Luoyang as the round altar; on the day of sacrifice the primogenitor Emperor Shun was paired; the offering stand bore raw fish, the pottery goblet held dark wine—if the gentry in silks had not held the guiding lines, who could have raised such things?
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 they raised a round mound on Mount Weisu south of Luoyang; at the offering the first ancestor Emperor Shun received joint worship, the stand carried uncooked fish, and earthen cups held unstrained wine—without belted officials to hold the ritual together, such a revival could never have happened.

sentences.zh: 宣景戎旅，未遑伊制。

translations.literal: During the military campaigns of Xuan and Jing, there was no leisure to institute this system.
translations.idiomatic: Under the martial reigns of the Xuan and Jing emperors there was no time to put this full program in place.

sentences.zh: 太康平吳，九州共一，禮經咸至，樂器同歸，於是齊魯諸生，各攜緗素。

translations.literal: When Taikang pacified Wu, the nine regions were one; ritual canons all arrived, musical instruments returned together, whereupon scholars of Qi and Lu each brought their silk-bound texts.
translations.idiomatic: After Taikang conquered Wu the realm was united; ritual manuals and bells and stones converged again, and classicists from Qi and Lu arrived bearing their silk-bound codices.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝亦初平寇亂，意先儀範。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu too, at first quelling banditry, put models and norms first.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, in the first rush of crushing rebellion, already put ceremony and precedent ahead of everything else.

sentences.zh: 其吉禮也，則三茅不翦，日觀停瑄；

translations.literal: In auspicious rites he did not trim the triple thatch, and halted the jade disk at Mount Ri;
translations.idiomatic: For felicitous sacrifice he left the triple thatch unshorn and stayed the jade regalia at Riguan;

sentences.zh: 其凶禮也，則深衣布冠，降席撤膳。

translations.literal: in inauspicious rites he wore deep garments and cloth caps, stepped down from mats, and cleared away viands.
translations.idiomatic: for mourning he donned plain robes and cloth caps, left his seat, and sent away the dishes.

sentences.zh: 明乎一謙三益之義，而教化行焉。

translations.literal: He made clear the meaning of “one yielding and three increases,” and transformation through instruction went forth.
translations.idiomatic: He spelled out the lesson of yielding once and gaining thrice over, and moral instruction could at last take hold.

sentences.zh: 元皇中興，事多權道，遺文舊典，不斷如發。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan restored the line, affairs mostly followed expediency; old writings and ancient canons hung by a hair’s breadth as if about to snap.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan revived the house, policy leaned on makeshifts; ancient statutes dangled by a thread, ready to break.

sentences.zh: 是以常侍戴邈詣闕上疏云：「方今天地更始，萬物權輿，蕩近世之流弊，創千齡之英範。

translations.literal: Therefore the permanent attendant Dai Miao came to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: “Now heaven and earth have begun anew, the myriad things are taking first steps; we should sweep away the abuses of recent ages and create a model splendid for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: So the palace attendant Dai Miao appeared at the gate with a memorial: “Heaven and earth have turned a fresh page and every creature is starting anew; we must wash away the stains of late decades and lay down a pattern worthy of a thousand-year reign.

sentences.zh: 是故雙劍之節崇，而飛白之俗成；

translations.literal: Therefore the etiquette of paired swords is honored, and the custom of flying-white script is established;
translations.idiomatic: Honor the discipline of the paired swords, and the fashion for feibai calligraphy will settle into custom;

sentences.zh: 挾琴之容飾，而赴曲之和作。

translations.literal: the bearing of cradling a lute is embellished, and the accord of performing a tune is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: refine the deportment of carrying the qin, and the harmony of answering the melody will follow.”

sentences.zh: 」其所以興起禮文，勸帝身先之也。

translations.literal: ” That is how he meant to promote ritual culture and urge the emperor to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: That was his way of stirring interest in ritual texts and asking the throne to show the way in person.

sentences.zh: 穆哀之後，王猷漸替，桓溫居揆，政由己出，而有司或曜斯文，增暉執事，主威長謝，臣道專行。

translations.literal: After Emperor Mu and Emperor Ai, royal governance gradually declined; Huan Wen held the chief ministry, government issued from himself alone, yet some offices still displayed this culture and lent luster to their duties—imperial authority long in eclipse, the way of ministers ran unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperors Mu and Ai, royal power thinned; Huan Wen seized the chief ministry and policy came from his hand alone, while some bureaus still paraded literary polish—sovereign prestige had long waned and ministerial will ran free.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰，「苟無其位，不可以作禮樂」，豈斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: The Record says, “If one lacks the position, one cannot make ritual and music”—does it not mean this?
translations.idiomatic: The Record warns, “Without the proper station you cannot enact ritual and music”—was it not pointing to exactly this?

sentences.zh: 晉始則有荀顗、鄭沖裁成國典，江左則有荀崧、刁協損益朝儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, Xun Yi and Zheng Chong shaped the state code; on the left bank of the river, Xun Song and Diao Xie revised court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin saw Xun Yi and Zheng Chong frame the national statutes; south of the river Xun Song and Diao Xie adjusted court ritual.

sentences.zh: 《周官》五禮，吉凶軍賓嘉，而吉禮之大，莫過祭祀，故《洪範》八政，三日祀。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou names five rituals—auspicious, inauspicious, military, guest, and festive—and among great auspicious rites none surpasses sacrifice, hence the Great Plan’s eight pursuits list sacrifice third.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou lists five kinds—auspicious, inauspicious, military, guest, and joyous—and of the great auspicious observances none tops sacrifice; that is why the “Great Plan” counts sacrifice third among its eight policies.

sentences.zh: 祀者，所以昭孝事祖，通於神明者也。

translations.literal: Sacrifice is the means by which one manifests filial service to ancestors and communicates with the numinous and enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice is how filial devotion to ancestors is made visible and how one reaches the spirits above.

sentences.zh: 漢興，承秦滅學之後，制度多未能復古。

translations.literal: When Han rose, inheriting after Qin’s destruction of learning, its institutions mostly failed to restore antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose on the ruins of Qin’s war on scholarship, its institutions seldom matched the old models.

sentences.zh: 曆東、西京四百餘年，故往往改變。

translations.literal: Across Eastern and Western Chang’an for over four hundred years, changes were often made.
translations.idiomatic: For more than four hundred years, through Western and Eastern capitals, those rules were repeatedly rewritten.

sentences.zh: 魏氏承漢末大亂，舊章殄滅，命侍中王粲、尚書衛顗草創朝儀。

translations.literal: Wei inherited the great chaos at Han’s end: old statutes were extinguished, and the court ordered Palace Attendant Wang Can and Minister Wei Gu to draft founding court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took over after Han’s final convulsions with classical law in ashes; the throne told palace attendant Wang Can and minister Wei Gu to sketch a court ritual from scratch.

sentences.zh: 及晉國建，文帝又命荀顗因魏代前事，撰為新禮，參考今古，更其節文，羊祜、任愷、庾峻、應貞並共刊定，成百六十五篇，奏之。

translations.literal: When the Jin state was established, Emperor Wen again ordered Xun Yi to follow Wei-era precedents and compile new ritual, consulting present and past and altering its articles; Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, and Ying Zhen jointly edited and fixed it into one hundred sixty-five pieces, which were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin realm was founded, Emperor Wen told Xun Yi to build on Wei precedents and draft a new ritual code, weighing ancient and recent usage and revising the clauses; Yang Hu, Ren Kai, Yu Jun, and Ying Zhen collated the text into 165 chapters for presentation.

sentences.zh: 太康初，尚書僕射硃整奏付尚書郎摯虞討論之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang, Minister Zhu Zheng memorialized to assign Junior Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhi Yu to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang Vice Director Zhu Zheng asked that Masters of Writing aide Zhi Yu be put in charge of reviewing it.

sentences.zh: 虞表所宜損增曰：

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial on what should be reduced or augmented, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu tabled his views on what to cut or add, stating:

sentences.zh: 臣典校故太尉顗所撰《五禮》，臣以為夫革命以垂統，帝王之美事也，隆禮以率教，邦國之大務也，是以臣前表禮事稽留，求速訖施行。

translations.literal: I was charged with collating the former Grand Commandant Yi’s compiled Five Rituals; I hold that reordering the mandate to hand down succession is a splendid thing for emperors and kings, and exalting ritual to lead instruction is the great task of states—hence my earlier memorial that ritual business had stalled, asking that it be quickly finished and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: I have been ordered to proof the Five Rituals compiled by the late Grand Commandant Xun Yi. A dynastic change that secures the line is a ruler’s finest achievement, and lifting ritual to teach the realm is a state’s first duty—hence my earlier plea that work on the code had stalled and ought to be finished and promulgated at once.

sentences.zh: 又以《喪服》最多疑闕，宜見補定。

translations.literal: I also hold that Mourning Dress has the most doubts and gaps and should be seen to with supplements and fixes.
translations.idiomatic: I also believe the Mourning Dress section holds the most unresolved questions and needs emendation.

sentences.zh: 又以今禮篇卷煩重，宜隨類通合。

translations.literal: I also hold that the present ritual in scrolls and fascicles is burdensomely heavy and should be merged by category in a connected way.
translations.idiomatic: I further argue that the present code is bloated with redundant fascicles and should be reorganized by topic into a leaner whole.

sentences.zh: 事久不出，懼見寢嘿。

translations.literal: The matter has long gone unresolved, and I fear it will fall silent and be shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Because it has dragged on so long, I worry the project will simply die in the files.

sentences.zh: 蓋冠婚祭會諸吉禮，其制少變；

translations.literal: In general for caps, weddings, sacrifices, and assemblies—the various auspicious rites—their forms change little;
translations.idiomatic: Capping, marriage, sacrifice, and public gatherings—the happy rites—vary only slightly in form;

sentences.zh: 至於《喪服》，世之要用，而特易失旨。

translations.literal: as for Mourning Dress, what the age most needs, it is especially easy to miss the point.
translations.idiomatic: mourning dress, which the world relies on daily, is the easiest place to lose the thread.

sentences.zh: 故子張疑高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂異父昆弟大功，而子夏謂之齊衰，及孔子沒而門人疑于所服。

translations.literal: Hence Zizhang doubted Gaozong’s three-year mourning in the silent hut; Zisi would not allow his son to wear mourning for a divorced mother; Ziyou said half-brothers by different fathers took great-grief cloth, but Zixia called it one-year cloth; when Confucius died his disciples quarreled over what garment to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zizhang questioned Shang’s three-year vigil; Zisi barred his son from mourning a mother cast out; Ziyou held that half-brothers of different fathers deserved dàgōng mourning while Zixia insisted on zīcuī; when Confucius passed away even his own students could not agree what robe to wear.

sentences.zh: 此等皆明達習禮，仰讀周典，俯師仲尼，漸漬聖訓，講肄積年，及遇喪事，尤尚若此，明喪禮易惑，不可不詳也。

translations.literal: These were all clear-sighted men versed in ritual who looked up to read the Zhou canons, looked down to take Confucius as teacher, steeped in sage instruction and debating many years—yet when they met bereavement they were still so—showing mourning ritual easily confuses and cannot but be treated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: They were acute scholars trained in ceremony, steeped in the Zhou odes and Confucius’s school—yet at a deathbed they still wavered, which shows how easily funeral rules confuse and how carefully they must be spelled out.

sentences.zh: 況自此已來，篇章焚散，去聖彌遠，喪制詭謬，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, since that time, chapters have been burnt and scattered, distance from the sages grows greater, and twisted mourning rules are only to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, texts have since been burned or lost, we stand further from the sages, and garbled mourning practice is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 是以《喪服》一卷，卷不盈握，而爭說紛然。

translations.literal: Hence one fascicle of Mourning Dress, not filling the hand, yet disputing explanations swarm.
translations.idiomatic: So a slim Mourning Dress fascicle, barely a handful thick, breeds endless wrangling.

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，鄭雲二十七月，王雲二十五月。

translations.literal: For three-year mourning Zheng says twenty-seven months, Wang says twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On the three-year term Zheng Xuan counts twenty-seven months, Wang Su twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 改葬之服，鄭雲服緦三月，王雲葬訖而除。

translations.literal: For reburial dress Zheng says wear finest hemp three months, Wang says remove when burial is done.
translations.idiomatic: On dress for reinterment Zheng prescribes sī hemp for three months, Wang ends mourning when the bones are settled.

sentences.zh: 繼母出嫁，鄭雲皆服，王雲從乎繼寄育乃為之服。

translations.literal: For stepmother remarrying out, Zheng says both wear mourning; Wang says only if one followed her in the foster care does one wear it.
translations.idiomatic: If a stepmother remarries away, Zheng demands mourning from both sons; Wang grants it only to a child she actually reared.

sentences.zh: 無服之殤，鄭雲子生一月哭之一日，王雲以哭之日易服之月。

translations.literal: For ungraded mourning for infants Zheng says for a child one month old mourn one day, Wang says use the day of crying for the month of changing dress.
translations.idiomatic: For infants who die without a named grade Zheng maps one day of weeping to a one-month baby, Wang swaps the “day of crying” for the month of garment change.

sentences.zh: 如此者甚眾。

translations.literal: Such cases are very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Examples could be multiplied at length.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》本文省略，必待注解事義乃彰；

translations.literal: The main text of Mourning Dress is abbreviated; one must await commentary for the meaning to appear clear;
translations.idiomatic: The classic Mourning Dress lines are terse; commentary is needed before they make sense;

sentences.zh: 其傳說差詳，世稱子夏所作。

translations.literal: its transmitted explanations are comparatively detailed; the age attributes them to Zixia’s authorship.
translations.idiomatic: the appended “traditions” are fuller, and tradition credits them to Zixia.

sentences.zh: 鄭王祖《經》宗《傳》，而各有異同，天下並疑，莫知所定，而顗直書古《經》文而已，盡除子夏《傳》及先儒注說，其事不可得行。

translations.literal: Zheng and Wang honored the classic and honored the commentary, yet each had divergences; all under heaven jointly doubted and knew not what to fix on, while Yi simply wrote the old classic text and utterly excised Zixia’s commentary and earlier Confucian glosses—such practice could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Wang each upheld text and subcommentary yet disagreed; the realm could not decide whom to follow, while Xun Yi simply copied the archaic classic, stripping Zixia’s gloss and older notes—an edition no one could actually perform.

sentences.zh: 及其行事，故當還頒異說，一彼一此，非所以定制也。

translations.literal: When it came to carrying it out, one would still have to promulgate competing theories, now this now that—not the means to fix a single standard.
translations.idiomatic: In practice officials would still circulate rival opinions, first one school then another—no way to establish a single rule.

sentences.zh: 臣以為今宜參采《禮記》，略取《傳》說，補其未備，一其殊義。

translations.literal: I hold that now we should consult the Record of Rites, broadly take the commentary’s explanations, fill what is not yet complete, and unify divergent meanings.
translations.idiomatic: I propose we mine the Book of Rites, adopt the clearest glosses, plug the gaps, and harmonize conflicting readings.

sentences.zh: 可依准王景侯所撰《喪服變除》，使類統明正，以斷疑爭，然後制無二門，咸同所由。

translations.literal: We may take as model Minister Wang Jinghou’s compiled Mourning Dress Transitions and Removals, making categories coherent and meanings plain to cut off doubtful disputes—only then will the system lack a double gate and all follow one source.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su’s Mourning Dress: Changes and Removals can supply the pattern—once categories read clearly, doubt dies and everyone walks one road through the gate.

sentences.zh: 又此禮當班於天下，不宜繁多。

translations.literal: Moreover this ritual should be promulgated through the realm and ought not be prolix.
translations.idiomatic: A code meant for the whole empire must not be wordy.

sentences.zh: 顗為百六十五篇，篇為一卷，合十五余萬言，臣猶謂卷多文煩，類皆重出。

translations.literal: Yi made one hundred sixty-five pieces, each piece one fascicle, totaling a little over one hundred fifty thousand graphs—even so I still say the scrolls are many and the text cumbersome, and that categories for the most part repeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi produced 165 chapters, one scroll each, totaling some 150,000 characters—yet even that feels heavy: too many fascicles say the same thing twice.

sentences.zh: 案《尚書·堯典》祀山川之禮，惟于東嶽備稱牲幣之數，陳所用之儀，其餘則但曰「如初」。

translations.literal: Examining the Canon of Yao in the Documents, the rite for sacrificing to mountains and streams only at the Eastern Marchmount fully names the number of victims and silks and sets out the observances used; for the rest it only says “as at first.”
translations.idiomatic: The “Canon of Yao” lists victims and silks in full only for the eastern peak; every other mountain sacrifice is dismissed with “do as before.”

sentences.zh: 《周禮》祀天地五帝享先王，其事同者皆曰「亦如之」，文約而義舉。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, for sacrificing to heaven and earth, the five emperors, and feasting former kings, where the affair is the same it always says “likewise”—the wording is spare but the meaning is brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ritual repeats “the same procedure” whenever heaven, earth, the five emperors, or royal ancestors share a step—brief language, complete sense.

sentences.zh: 今禮儀事同而名異者，輒別為篇，卷煩而不典。

translations.literal: Now where ritual practice is the same but the titles differ, each is split into a separate piece—scrolls are cumbersome and not exemplary.
translations.idiomatic: Our draft gives a new chapter whenever the label changes though the act is identical—fat, inelegant, and hard to use.

sentences.zh: 皆宜省文通事，隨類合之，事有不同，乃列其異。

translations.literal: All should trim wording to connect the matter, combine by kind, and only when the affair differs list the difference.
translations.idiomatic: We should prune verbiage, merge like with like, and note exceptions only where the rite truly changes.

sentences.zh: 如此，所減三分之一。

translations.literal: In this way one may reduce by one third.
translations.idiomatic: That alone could cut the bulk by a third.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和元年正月丁未，郊祀武帝以配天，宗祀文帝於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wei Emperor Ming’s Taihe, first month day dingwei, he suburban-sacrificed to Emperor Wu to match heaven, and in the Bright Hall veneratively sacrificed to Emperor Wen to match the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi’s Taihe 1, day dingwei of the first month: a suburban offering paired Emperor Wu with Heaven; in the Bright Hall an honoring sacrifice paired Emperor Wen with the Supreme God.

sentences.zh: 於是時，二漢郊禋之制具存，魏所損益可知。

translations.literal: At that time the two-Han suburban-sacrifice system remained complete, and what Wei added or subtracted can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Western and Eastern Han precedents were still intact, so Wei’s tweaks are easy to trace.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，天子東巡，過繁昌，使執金吾臧霸行太尉事，以特牛祠受禪壇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, eighth month, the Son of Heaven toured east, passed Fanchang, and ordered Bearer of the Golden Mace Zang Ba to act as Grand Commandant and sacrifice a special ox at the abdication altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, eighth month, the emperor traveled east through Fanchang and told the chief of police Zang Ba to stand in as Grand Commandant and offer a singled-out ox at the abdication terrace.

sentences.zh: 景初元年十月乙卯，始營洛陽南委粟山為圜丘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month day yimao of Jingchu year 1, they first built south of Luoyang Mount Weisu as the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 1, tenth month, day yimao: work began on a round altar on Mount Weisu south of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔漢氏之初，承秦滅學之後，采摭殘缺，以備郊祀。

translations.literal: An edict said: “In the beginning of the Han, following Qin’s destruction of learning, they gathered damaged remains to complete suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: “Early Han, picking through Qin’s wreckage of the classics, patched missing pieces to keep suburban worship alive.

sentences.zh: 自甘泉后土，雍宮五畤，神祗百萬位元，多不經見，並以興廢無常，一彼一此，四百餘年，廢無禘禮，古代之所更立者，遂有闕焉。

translations.literal: From Sweet Springs and the Earth Altar at Yong’s five shrines, the positions of the hundred thousand spirits mostly were not seen in the classics, and because rise and fall lacked constancy, now this now that, for four hundred more years the grand di sacrifice lapsed; what the ancients had renewed in turn had gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Between Sweet Springs, the Yong earth altar, and the five shrines, countless spirit seats lacked canonical warrant; cults rose and fell at whim, and for four centuries the great di sacrifice disappeared—lines the ancients had carefully restored were left broken.

sentences.zh: 曹氏世系，出自有虞氏。

translations.literal: The Cao lineage traces to Youyu’s clan.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Cao claims descent from the line of Shun of Youyu.

sentences.zh: 今祀圜丘以始祖帝舜配，號圜丘曰皇皇帝天。

translations.literal: Now at the round mound we sacrifice with primogenitor Emperor Shun as counterpart, hailing the round mound as August August Emperor Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the round altar honors Supreme Heaven as “August August Emperor Heaven,” with first ancestor Emperor Shun as correlative.

sentences.zh: 方丘所祭曰皇皇后地，以舜妃伊氏配。

translations.literal: What the square mound sacrifices is called August August Queen Earth, with Shun’s consort surnamed Yi as counterpart.
translations.idiomatic: The square altar addresses “August August Queen Earth,” paired with Shun’s consort of the Yi clan.

sentences.zh: 天郊所祭曰皇天之神，以太祖武皇帝配。

translations.literal: What the heaven suburb sacrifices is called God of August Heaven, with Founding Emperor Wu as counterpart.
translations.idiomatic: The southern suburb names the spirit “God of August Heaven,” with dynastic founder Emperor Wu as partner.

sentences.zh: 地郊所祭曰皇地之祗，以武宣皇后配。

translations.literal: What the earth suburb sacrifices is called Earth numen of August Earth, with Empress Wuxuan as counterpart.
translations.idiomatic: The northern suburb names “Numen of August Earth,” partnered by Empress Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 宗祀皇考高祖文皇帝于明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: In the Bright Hall we honor father August Gaozu Wendi to match the Supreme Lord.”
translations.idiomatic: Inside the Bright Hall we revere Imperial Father Gaozu Wendi as correlative to the Supreme God.”

sentences.zh: 」十二月壬子冬至，始祀皇皇帝天於圜丘，以始祖有虞帝舜配。

translations.literal: ” On the renzi day of the twelfth month, winter solstice, they first sacrificed to August August Emperor Heaven at the round mound, with primogenitor Youyu Emperor Shun as counterpart.
translations.idiomatic: Closing the edict—on winter solstice, day renzi of the twelfth month, the court first worshiped “August August Emperor Heaven” on the round mound with Shun of Youyu as joint honoree.

sentences.zh: 自正始以後，終魏世不復郊祀。

translations.literal: From Zhengshi onward through the end of Wei they never again performed suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengshi era Wei abandoned suburban sacrifice entirely.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙二年十二月甲子，使持節侍中太保鄭沖、兼太尉司隸校尉李憙奉皇帝璽綬策書，禪位於晉。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Yuan’s second Xixi year, twelfth month day jiazi, Commissioner Bearing Insignia, Palace Attendant, Grand Guardian Zheng Chong, and concurrently Grand Commandant, Metropolitan Superintendent Li Xi presented the imperial seal-cord and abdication document and yielded the throne to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuandi, Xixi 2, day jiazi of the twelfth month: credential-bearing attendant-grand tutor Zheng Chong and acting grand commandant Li Xi, also metropolitan commandant, delivered the seal-straps and abdication edict, ceding the mandate to Jin.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，武皇帝設壇場于南郊，柴燎告類於上帝，是時尚未有祖配。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Emperor Wu set up an altar field south of the suburb and burned reeds in announcement of category to the Supreme Lord; at that time there was not yet an ancestor counterpart.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Emperor Wu of Jin laid out a southern suburban precinct, burned kindling, and reported the dynastic change to Heaven; no ancestor shared the offering yet.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月，詔曰：「有司前奏郊祀權用魏禮，朕不慮改作之難，令便為永制，眾議紛互，遂不時定，不得以時供饗神祗，配以祖考。

translations.literal: In Taishi second year first month an edict said: “The offices earlier memorialized that suburban sacrifice provisionally used Wei ritual; I did not reckon the hardship of reform, and let it at once become perpetual usage—opinions clashed and it was not settled in good time, so we could not in season offer to spirits and pair with forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 2, first month: an edict read, “Officials asked to keep Wei’s provisional suburban form; I underestimated how hard true reform would be and let it stand as permanent—debate gridlocked, deadlines slipped, and heaven and the ancestors went unserved on schedule.

sentences.zh: 日夕難企，貶食忘安，其便郊祀。

translations.literal: Sunset hard to await, I cut my fare and forget ease—now let suburban sacrifice proceed.”
translations.idiomatic: Days grow short while I wait; I have trimmed my meals and lost rest—authorize the suburban rite at once.”

sentences.zh: 」時群臣又議，五帝即天也，王氣時異，故殊其號，雖名有五，其實一神。

translations.literal: The ministers then debated: the Five Emperors are heaven; royal qi differed by season, hence their titles differed; though the names are five, in reality it is one spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued that the Five Emperors are simply aspects of Heaven: the royal qi shifted with the seasons, so the titles multiplied, yet only one god stood behind them.

sentences.zh: 明堂南郊，宜除五帝之坐，五郊改五精之號，皆同稱昊天上帝，各設一坐而已。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall and southern suburb the seats of the Five Emperors should be removed; the five suburbs should change the names of the five essences—all should equally be called August Heaven Emperor, each receiving only one seat.
translations.idiomatic: They urged removing the five thrones from the Bright Hall and southern altar, renaming the five directional gods as five essences of the single “August Heaven Emperor,” each with one seat.

sentences.zh: 地郊又除先後配祀。

translations.literal: At the earth suburb remove pairing sacrifices to former empresses.
translations.idiomatic: At the earth altar drop the joint offerings to late empresses.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted every point.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，郊禮宣皇帝以配天，宗祀文皇帝于明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: Second month dingchou, suburban rite paired Emperor Xuan with heaven; in the Bright Hall the venerative rite paired Emperor Wen with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day dingchou: the suburban cult paired Emperor Xuan with Heaven; the Bright Hall cult paired Emperor Wen with the Supreme God.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，有司又議奏，古者丘郊不異，宜並圓丘方丘於南北郊，更修立壇兆，其二至之祀合於二郊。

translations.literal: That year eleventh month the offices again debated and memorialized: in antiquity round mound and suburb did not differ; it is fitting to join round mound and square mound at south and north suburbs and anew build altar foundations, and the two solstice sacrifices should unite with the two suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month of the same year: officials revisited the issue—classically the mound rite and suburban rite were one; they proposed combining round and square altars with the south and north suburban sites and rebuilding the platforms so winter and summer solstice offerings matched the twin suburbs.

sentences.zh: 帝又從之，一如宣帝所用王肅議也。

translations.literal: The emperor again followed it, entirely as the counsel Wang Su used under Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed again, adopting in full the program Wang Su had once urged on Emperor Xuan of Wei.

sentences.zh: 是月庚寅冬至，帝親祠圓丘於南郊。

translations.literal: That month gengyin, winter solstice, the emperor in person sacrificed at the round mound south of the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: That month, winter solstice on gengyin, the sovereign personally worshiped at the southern suburban round altar.

sentences.zh: 自是後，圓丘方澤不別立。

translations.literal: From this on round mound and square marsh were not separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward no separate round mound or square pool stood apart from those suburban sites.

sentences.zh: 太康三年正月，帝親郊祀，皇太子、皇子悉侍祠。

translations.literal: Taikang third year first month, the emperor in person performed suburban sacrifice; the heir apparent and imperial sons all attended sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 3, first month: the emperor led the suburban sacrifice in person, with the crown prince and all imperial sons assisting at the offerings.

sentences.zh: 十年十月，又詔曰：「《孝經》'郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, tenth month, an edict again said: “The Classic of Filial Piety states, “In suburban sacrifice Hou Ji was paired with Heaven; in the Bright Hall King Wen was honored to match the Supreme Lord.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict in the tenth month of the tenth year quoted the Classic of Filial Piety: suburban worship joined Hou Ji to Heaven, while the Bright Hall cult joined King Wen to the high god.

sentences.zh: '而《周官》雲'祀天旅上帝'，又曰'祀地旅四望'。

translations.literal: ” yet the Offices of Zhou says “sacrifice to Heaven and marshal the Supreme Lord,” and also says “sacrifice to Earth and marshal the four wang.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou adds that heaven is worshiped by “marshaling” the high god and earth by “marshaling” the four directional vistas.

sentences.zh: 望非地，則明堂上帝不得為天也。

translations.literal: If wang is not earth, then the Supreme Lord of the Bright Hall cannot be Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since the “four wang” are not simply “earth,” the “Supreme Lord” honored in the Bright Hall cannot be the same as “Heaven” at the mound altar.

sentences.zh: 往者眾議除明堂五帝位，考之禮文不正。

translations.literal: Previously the assembly removed the Five Emperors’ seats from the Bright Hall—examining the ritual texts shows that was incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier decision to strip the Five Thrones from the Bright Hall does not hold up when checked against canonical wording.

sentences.zh: 且《詩序》曰'文武之功，起於後稷'，故推以配天焉。

translations.literal: Moreover the Preface to the Odes says “The achievements of Wen and Wu began with Hou Ji,” hence he is exalted to pair with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes preface traces King Wen’s and King Wu’s merit to Hou Ji, which is why he ranks as heaven’s partner.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以神武創業，既已配天，復以先帝配天，於義亦所不安。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan founded the enterprise with divine martial prowess—already paired with Heaven—yet again pairing a former emperor with Heaven is not right in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan’s martial founding already earned him a share of heaven; adding another dynastic father to the same honor upsets the logic of the pairing.

sentences.zh: 其復明堂及南郊五帝位。

translations.literal: Let the Bright Hall and the Five Emperors’ seats at the southern suburb be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the Bright Hall layout and the five thrones at the southern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 湣帝都長安，未及立郊廟而敗。

translations.literal: Emperor Min ruled from Chang’an but fell before suburban and temple shrines could be erected.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min never finished founding suburban and ancestral shrines at Chang’an before his line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 元帝渡江，太興二年始議立郊祀儀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, in Taixing 2 they first debated establishing suburban rite.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled south, Taixing 2 opened discussion on how to stage suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尚書令刁協、國子祭酒杜夷議，宜須旋都洛邑乃修之。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Xie and libationer Du Yi argued one must wait until the capital returned to Luoyang to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie and Du Yi insisted work should wait until the throne moved back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 司徒荀組據漢獻帝都許即便立郊，自宜於此修奉。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Xun Zu cited that when Han Xiandi resided at Xu they immediately set up suburbs—here too they ought to maintain the cult.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu countered with Han Xiandi’s example: suburbs were raised at Xu on short notice, so Jiangnan could do the same.

sentences.zh: 驃騎王導、僕射荀崧、太常華恆、中書侍郎庾亮皆同組議，事遂施行，立南郊於已地。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao, Director Xun Song, Chamberlain Hua Heng, and palace secretary Yu Liang all concurred with Zu; the plan went forward and the southern suburb was sited on the ji quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, Xun Song, Hua Heng, and Yu Liang sided with Xun Zu, the southern altar was dedicated on ji ground.

sentences.zh: 其制度皆太常賀循所定，多依漢及晉初之儀。

translations.literal: The regulations were all fixed by Chamberlain He Xun, largely following Han and early Jin practice.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun drafted the liturgy, borrowing heavily from Western Han and Western Jin forms.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯，帝親郊祀，饗配之禮一依武帝始郊故事。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinmao, the emperor suburban-sacrificed in person; the feast and pairing rites followed Emperor Wu’s first suburban precedent in every point.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the third month the sovereign led the suburban offering himself, matching Emperor Wu’s inaugural southern rite.

sentences.zh: 是時尚未立北壇，地祗眾神共在天郊。

translations.literal: At that time the northern platform was not yet built; earth numina and the host of spirits shared the heaven altar.
translations.idiomatic: With no northern altar yet, chthonic gods were crowded into the sky-cult precinct.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧三年七月，始詔立北郊，未及建而帝崩。

translations.literal: Mingdi, Taining 3, seventh month, first ordered a northern suburb—not built before the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi authorized a northern site in Taining 3 but died before builders finished.

sentences.zh: 及成帝咸和八年正月，追述前旨，于覆舟山南立之。

translations.literal: When Chengdi, Xianhe 8 first month, carried out the earlier intent, they erected it south of Mount Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi revived the project in Xianhe 8, placing the altar south of Mount Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 天郊則五帝之佐、日月、五星、二十八宿、文昌、北斗、三台、司命、軒轅、后土、太一、天一、太微、句陳、北極、雨師、雷電、司空、風伯、老人，凡六十二神也。

translations.literal: At the heaven suburb were assistants to the Five Emperors, sun and moon, five planets, twenty-eight lodges, Wenchang, Northern Dipper, Three Platforms, Siming, Xuanyuan, Houtu, Taiyi, Tianyi, Taiwei, Gouchen, pole star, rain master, thunder and lightning, Sikong, wind elder, and elder star—sixty-two spirits in all.
translations.idiomatic: The southern roster listed the five celestial hosts’ aides, luminaries, constellations, polar asterisms, weather gods, and more—sixty-two seats.

sentences.zh: 地郊則五嶽、四望、四海、四瀆、五湖、五帝之佐、沂山、岳山、白山、霍山、醫無閭山、蔣山、松江、會稽山、錢唐江、先農，凡四十四神也。

translations.literal: At the earth suburb were the five marchmounts, four wang, four seas, four great rivers, five lakes, assistants to the Five Emperors, Mount Yi, Mount Yue, Mount Bai, Mount Huo, Mount Yiwulu, Mount Jiang, the Song, Mount Kuaiji, the Qiantang, and First Farmer—forty-four spirits in all.
translations.idiomatic: The northern roster covered mountains, rivers, lakes, and the spirit of the plow—forty-four names.

sentences.zh: 江南諸小山，蓋江左所立，猶如漢西京關中小水皆有祭秩也。

translations.literal: The lesser hills south of the Yangzi were erected under the eastern court, just as at Western Han’s Guanzhong every minor stream held a graded offering.
translations.idiomatic: Small Jiangnan peaks received shrines the way Guanzhong’s brooks did in Chang’an days.

sentences.zh: 是月辛未，祀北郊，始以宣穆張惶後配，此魏氏故事，非晉舊也。

translations.literal: That month, day xinwei, they sacrificed at the northern suburb, pairing for the first time Empress Xuanmu of the Zhang clan—Wei precedent, not original Jin usage.
translations.idiomatic: The xinwei offering introduced Empress Xuanmu Zhang as earth’s consort, copying Wei rather than Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 康帝建元元年正月，將北郊，有疑議。

translations.literal: Kangdi, Jianyuan 1 first month, as they were about to hold the northern suburb, doubts arose.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangdi prepared a northern rite in Jianyuan 1, officials quarreled over details.

sentences.zh: 太常顧和表：「泰始中，合二至之禮於二郊。

translations.literal: Chamberlain Gu He submitted: “Under Taishi the two solstice ceremonies were merged into the twin suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He’s memorial recalled Taishi reforms that folded both solstices into the paired suburban sites.

sentences.zh: 北郊之月，古無明文，或以夏至，或同用陽月。

translations.literal: For the northern month antiquity gives no explicit text—some use summer solstice, some share the yang month with the south.
translations.idiomatic: Classics never pin the northern date—some argued midsummer, others the same yang-month slot as the south.

sentences.zh: 漢光武正月辛未，始建北郊，此則與南郊同月。

translations.literal: Han Guangwu on first month day xinwei first built the northern suburb, so it shared the month with the southern.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu’s first northern altar fell on xinwei of the first month, matching the southern calendar.

sentences.zh: 及中興草創，百度從簡，合七郊於一丘，憲章未備，權用斯禮，蓋時宜也。

translations.literal: At the restoration’s founding, every regulation was simplified; seven suburban sites were folded into one mound; the code was unfinished and this expedient was used—it suited the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern exile had collapsed seven cults into one hill for lack of statutes—an emergency measure.

sentences.zh: 至咸和中，議別立北郊，同用正月。

translations.literal: By Xianhe they debated a separate northern altar, still using the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe discussions split the altars yet kept the first-month timing.

sentences.zh: 魏承後漢，正月祭天以地配。

translations.literal: Wei inherited Later Han: first-month heaven sacrifice paired earth.
translations.idiomatic: Wei followed Eastern Han in pairing earth with a first-month heaven offering.

sentences.zh: 時高堂隆等以為禮祭天不以地配，而稱《周禮》三王之郊一用夏正。

translations.literal: Then Gao Tanglong and others held that ritual law forbids pairing earth with heaven sacrifice, citing the Rites of Zhou that the three kings’ suburbs always used the Xia calendar’s first month.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong cited Zhou precedent that heaven stands alone at suburb and that true kings use the Xia-style opening month.

sentences.zh: 」於是從和議。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they followed He’s recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Gu He’s line.

sentences.zh: 是月辛未南郊，辛已北郊，帝皆親奉。

translations.literal: That month, day xinwei at the southern suburb and day xinsi at the northern, the emperor personally led both.
translations.idiomatic: He presided in person at southern xinwei and northern xinsi the same month.

sentences.zh: 安帝元興三年，劉裕討桓玄，走之。

translations.literal: Andi, Yuanxing 3, Liu Yu campaigned against Huan Xuan and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing 3 Liu Yu expelled Huan Xuan from the capital region.

sentences.zh: 已卯，告義功於南郊。

translations.literal: Day jimao, he reported the righteous victory at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he announced the punitive success before the southern altar.

sentences.zh: 是年，帝蒙塵江陵未反。

translations.literal: That year the emperor remained stranded at Jiangling and had not returned.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was still exiled at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 其明年應郊，朝議以為宜依《周禮》，宗伯攝職，三公行事。

translations.literal: The next year suburban sacrifice fell due; court opinion held one should follow the Rites of Zhou and let the Minister of Heaven stand in while the three dukes officiate.
translations.idiomatic: When the next annual rite came due, ministers wanted the Zhou model: the Minister of Rites as proxy, the three excellencies conducting the liturgy.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞王納之獨曰：「既殯郊祀，自是天子當陽，有君存焉，稟命而行，何所辯也。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Nazhi alone said: “Once the bier stands and suburban worship is scheduled, the Son of Heaven by rights faces south—a ruler still sits the throne; agents simply carry his order—what is left to argue?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Nazhi objected: the embalmed sovereign still reigns in name, so ministers act on mandate; proxy sacrifice needs no further plea.

sentences.zh: 郊之興否，豈如今日之比乎！

translations.literal: Whether suburb proceeds cannot be compared to today’s situation!
translations.idiomatic: This is not like ordinary times when the throne sits empty.

sentences.zh: 」議者又云：「今宜郊，故是承制所得令三公行事。

translations.literal: ” Others said: “Suburb is proper now, hence by received edict the three dukes may perform it.
translations.idiomatic: Critics answered that current edicts already empower the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 」又「郊天極尊，惟一而已，故非天子不祀也。

translations.literal: ” Moreover “suburban heaven is supremely exalted—only one cult—hence none but the Son of Heaven may offer.”
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s suburban altar is uniquely august—only the emperor may approach it.

sentences.zh: 庶人以上，莫不蒸嘗，嫡子居外，介子執事，未有不親受命而可祭天者。

translations.literal: Everyone below the nobility performs seasonal steam offerings; when the heir is abroad and a younger son conducts the rite, never may one sacrifice to heaven without personally receiving the command.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser kin offer at home shrines, but heaven demands the ruler’s own warrant.

sentences.zh: 」納之又曰：「武皇受禪，用二月郊，元帝中興，以三月郊。

translations.literal: ” Nazhi added: “When Wu of Jin received the mandate he suburban-sacrificed in the second month; when Yuan restored the line he used the third.
translations.idiomatic: Wang added that Jin Wu used the second month and Yuan the third for their first suburbs.

sentences.zh: 今郊時未過，日望輿駕，無為欲速，而使皇輿旋反，更不得親奉也。

translations.literal: The suburban season is not yet past; we still await the imperial carriage—do not rush and make the court return only to deny the emperor personal attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar still allows the true sovereign to arrive in time; haste would cheat him of the rite.

sentences.zh: 」於是從納之議。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they followed Nazhi’s opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The throne took Wang Nazhi’s side.

sentences.zh: 郊廟牲幣璧玉之色，雖有成文，秦世多以騮駒，漢則但雲犢，未辯其色。

translations.literal: For suburban and temple victims, silks, disks, and jade colors canonical texts exist, yet Qin often used bay colts while Han merely says “calves,” not clarifying color.
translations.idiomatic: Classical rules name victim hues, but Qin favored bay foals and Han spoke only of “calves.”

sentences.zh: 江左南北郊同用玄牲，明堂廟社同以赤牲。

translations.literal: South of the river both south and north suburbs used black victims; Bright Hall, temples, and soil altars all used red victims.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin used black oxen at both suburbs and red at Bright Hall, shrines, and earth gods.

sentences.zh: 禮，有事告祖禰宜社之文，未有告郊之典也。

translations.literal: Rite prescribes reporting great affairs to ancestors and to the soil god—no canon for reporting to the suburban heaven altar.
translations.idiomatic: Classics tell ministers to notify ancestral shrines and the she altar, not the suburban mound.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，天子之喪，使太尉告諡于南郊，他無聞焉。

translations.literal: Han observance: on a Son of Heaven’s death the Grand Commandant announced his posthumous title at the southern suburb—nothing else is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Han only notes the grand commandant proclaiming the temple name south of the city.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年七月，帝將東巡，以大軍當出，使太常以一特牛告祠南郊。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu 4 seventh month, about to tour east because a great army would march, ordered the chamberlain to announce one special ox at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi before an eastern campaign had a single ox reported at the southern altar.

sentences.zh: 及文帝崩，太尉鐘繇告諡南郊，皆是有事於郊也。

translations.literal: When Wendi died, Grand Commandant Zhong Yao announced his posthumous title at the southern suburb—both were suburban business.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao’s posthumous proclamation for Cao Pi was likewise a southern-suburb affair.

sentences.zh: 江左則廢。

translations.literal: South of the river the practice was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Jin abandoned it after crossing the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 禮，春分祀朝日于東，秋分祀夕月於西。

translations.literal: Rite: at spring equinox sacrifice to the morning sun in the east; at autumn equinox sacrifice to the evening moon in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Canon fixes vernal equinox dawn rites eastward and autumnal dusk rites westward.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝郊泰畤，平旦出竹宮，東向揖日，其夕西向揖月。

translations.literal: Han Wudi at the Tai suburb, at dawn left the bamboo palace, bowed east to the sun; that evening bowed west to the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi left his bamboo lodge before sunrise to salute the sun eastward and the moon westward the same night.

sentences.zh: 既郊明，又不在東西郊也。

translations.literal: Having suburban-sacrificed at dawn, he was no longer at the eastern or western suburban sites.
translations.idiomatic: Those bows happened at Tai, not at dedicated east-west altars.

sentences.zh: 後遂旦夕常拜。

translations.literal: Later they bowed morning and evening as routine.
translations.idiomatic: Later emperors bowed twice daily by habit.

sentences.zh: 故魏文帝詔曰：「漢氏不拜日於東郊，而旦夕常于殿下東西拜日月，煩褻似家人之事，非事天神之道也。

translations.literal: Hence Wei Wendi’s edict: “Han did not salute the sun at the eastern suburb but morning and evening bowed to sun and moon below the hall east and west—fussy and familiar like a household chore, not the way to serve heaven’s gods.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi complained that Han’s hallway bows looked domestic, not celestial.

sentences.zh: 」黃初二年正月乙亥，祀朝日於東門之外，又違禮二分之義。

translations.literal: ” Huangchu 2 first month, day yihai, he sacrificed to the morning sun outside the east gate—again violating the equinox rule.
translations.idiomatic: His Huangchu 2 eastern-gate sun rite ignored the true equinox timing.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和元年二月丁亥，祀朝日於東郊，八月己丑，祀夕月於西郊，始得古禮。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi, Taihe 1 second month day dinghai sacrificed to the morning sun at the eastern suburb; eighth month day jichou sacrificed to the evening moon at the western suburb—then ancient rite was attained.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi restored east and west suburban equinox observances in Taihe 1.

sentences.zh: 及武帝太康二年，有司奏，春分依舊請車駕祀朝日，寒溫未適，可不親出。

translations.literal: When Jin Wudi, Taikang 2, the offices memorialized: at spring equinox as before request the imperial carriage to sacrifice to the morning sun—cold and heat may be unsuitable, so the sovereign need not go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 2 officials asked to skip the emperor’s vernal equinox trip if weather disagreed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「禮儀宜有常，若如所奏，與故太尉所撰不同，復為無定制也。

translations.literal: Edict: “Ritual ought to be regular; if we follow your memorial it differs from what the late grand commandant compiled and again leaves us without a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi replied that wavering from the codex leaves no stable custom.

sentences.zh: 間者方難未平，故每從所奏，今戎事弭息，惟此為大。

translations.literal: Lately rebellion was still unsettled, so I often assented; now war has quieted—this matter matters most.
translations.idiomatic: He had indulged shortcuts during rebellion; peace demanded consistency.

sentences.zh: 」案此詔，帝復為親祀朝日也。

translations.literal: ” Examining this edict, the emperor again performed the morning sun sacrifice in person.
translations.idiomatic: The edict shows he resumed personal equinox worship.

sentences.zh: 此後廢。

translations.literal: Afterward it lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Later courts let it die out.

sentences.zh: 晉初以文帝配，後復以宣帝，尋復還以文帝配，其餘無所變革。

translations.literal: At Jin’s beginning Emperor Wen was paired; later again Emperor Xuan, soon reverted to Emperor Wen for pairing; otherwise nothing changed.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin rotated heaven’s partner between Wendi and Xuandi, then settled back on Wendi.

sentences.zh: 是則郊與明堂，同配異配，參差不同矣。

translations.literal: Thus suburban altar and Bright Hall sometimes shared a partner, sometimes differed—inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and Bright Hall pairings therefore never quite matched.

sentences.zh: 摯虞議以為：「漢魏故事，明堂祀五帝之神。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu argued: “Han-Wei precedent had the Bright Hall worship the Five Emperors’ spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu noted old Bright Hall cults honored five celestial lords.

sentences.zh: 新禮，五帝即上帝，即天帝也。

translations.literal: The new ritual treats the Five Emperors as the Supreme Lord—that is, as heaven itself.
translations.idiomatic: The new code collapsed them into the single high god.

sentences.zh: 明堂除五帝之位，惟祭上帝。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall removes the Five Emperors’ seats and worships only the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Reform stripped the five thrones, leaving one high god.

sentences.zh: 案仲尼稱'郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: Yet Zhongni said “In suburban sacrifice Hou Ji was paired with Heaven; in the Bright Hall King Wen was honored to match the Supreme Lord.”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius still distinguished mound heaven from Bright Hall’s “Supreme Lord.”

sentences.zh: '《周禮》，祀天旅上帝，祀地旅四望。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: sacrifice to heaven and marshal the Supreme Lord; sacrifice to earth and marshal the four wang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou text pairs “marshaling heaven” with the high god and earth with the four vistas.

sentences.zh: 望非地，則上帝非天，斷可識矣。

translations.literal: If wang is not earth, then the Supreme Lord is not heaven—this can be decided clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Once “wang” is not mere soil, “Supreme Lord” cannot equal “Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 郊丘之祀，掃地而祭，牲用繭栗，器用陶匏，事反其始，故配以遠祖。

translations.literal: Suburban mound sacrifice sweeps the ground for the offering, uses cocoon and chestnut victims, pottery and gourd vessels—returning to beginnings—hence pairing uses a remote ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The open-air mound uses simplest vessels and far ancestors to echo origins.

sentences.zh: 明堂之祭，備物以薦，玉牲並陳，籩豆成列，禮同人鬼，故配以近考。

translations.literal: Bright Hall sacrifice lays out full vessels, jade and victims together, baskets and tureens in rows—rites like those for human ghosts—hence pairing uses a recent forebear.
translations.idiomatic: The hall’s rich spread resembles ancestral shrines, so a nearer father joins the god.

sentences.zh: 郊堂百萬位元，居然異體，牲牢品物，質文殊趣。

translations.literal: Suburban hall and altar host myriad seats of clearly different bodies; victims and vessels differ in substance and ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The two venues, offerings, and regalia diverge sharply.

sentences.zh: 且祖考同配，非謂尊嚴之美，三日再祀，非謂不黷之義，其非一神，亦足明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover sharing one partner for both is not about maximizing dignity, and sacrificing twice in three days is not about avoiding redundancy—enough to show they are not one spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Dual pairing and repeated offerings within days prove two distinct divinities.

sentences.zh: 昔在上古，生為明王，沒則配五行，故太昊配木，神農配火，少昊配金，顓頊配水，黃帝配土。

translations.literal: In high antiquity, while alive they were enlightened kings; dead they matched the five phases—hence Taihao with wood, Shennong with fire, Shaohao with metal, Zhuanxu with water, Huangdi with earth.
translations.idiomatic: Archaic sage-kings became phase patrons after death.

sentences.zh: 此五帝者，配天之神，同兆之於四郊，報之於明堂。

translations.literal: These Five Emperors are gods who pair with heaven; they share omens at the four suburbs and receive thanks in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those five powers answer heaven at the directional altars and the hall.

sentences.zh: 祀天，大裘而冕，祀五帝亦如之。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to heaven, great fur robe and crown; sacrificing to the Five Emperors likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and the five hosts share the same grand fur regalia.

sentences.zh: 或以為五精之帝，佐天育物者也。

translations.literal: Some hold they are the five essence emperors who assist heaven in nurturing things.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators call them the five “quintessence” spirits aiding heaven’s nurture.

sentences.zh: 前代相因，莫之或廢，晉初始從異議。

translations.literal: Earlier dynasties inherited this without abolishing it; Western Jin at first followed the dissenting view.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held until early Jin innovators disagreed.

sentences.zh: 《庚午詔書》，明堂及南郊除五帝之位，惟祀天神，新禮奉而用之。

translations.literal: The gengwu edict removed Five Emperor seats from Bright Hall and southern suburb, worshiping only the celestial god; the new ritual adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The gengwu reform cleared five thrones for a single sky god.

sentences.zh: 前太醫令韓楊上書，宜如舊祀五帝。

translations.literal: Former court physician Han Yang memorialized to restore Five Emperor worship as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yang asked to revive the five-lord cult.

sentences.zh: 太康十年，詔已施用。

translations.literal: Taikang 10 edict: already put in force.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 10 made it policy.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，明堂及郊祀五帝如舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the new ritual: Bright Hall and suburban sacrifice to the Five Emperors as before.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial urged codifying the old five-god pattern for hall and suburb.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ” The edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 江左以後，未遑修建。

translations.literal: After crossing the river they had no leisure to build.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin never reconstructed it amid turmoil.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，太史每歲上其年曆，先立春、立夏、大暑、立秋、立冬常讀五時令，皇帝所服，各隨五時之色。

translations.literal: Han observance: each year the grand astrologer presented the calendar; before spring establishment, summer establishment, great heat, autumn establishment, and winter establishment they routinely read the five seasonal mandates; the emperor’s garments followed each season’s color.
translations.idiomatic: Han astrologers issued calendars and, before five seasonal nodes, read the “five commands” while the sovereign shifted robe colors.

sentences.zh: 帝升御坐，尚書令以下就席位，尚書三公郎以令置案上，奉以入，就席伏讀訖，賜酒一卮。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the throne; below the director of the Masters of Writing took seats; Masters of Writing aides for the three excellencies placed the mandate on the desk, bore it in, took seat, knelt and read it through, then received one cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Officials entered with the written command, read it kneeling, and drank a ritual cup.

sentences.zh: 魏氏常行其禮。

translations.literal: Wei routinely performed this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei kept the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年，通事白曰：「前後但見讀春夏秋冬四時令，至於服黃之時，獨闕不讀，今不解其故。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi, Jingchu 1, the liaison reported: “Previously we only heard the spring, summer, autumn, and winter mandates read; for the yellow-garment season alone nothing was read—we do not understand why.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk noted Wei never read a “great heat” yellow-season edict.

sentences.zh: 」散騎常侍領太史令高堂隆以為「黃於五行，中央土也，王四季各十八日。

translations.literal: ” Cavalier attendant concurrent grand astrologer Gao Tanglong held that “yellow in the five phases is central earth; the king governs eighteen days in each of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong explained earth’s central yellow patch inside each season.

sentences.zh: 土生於火，故於火用事之末服黃，三季則否。

translations.literal: Earth is born from fire, hence yellow garments follow the fire season’s end; the other three seasons do not.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow robes close the “fire” fortnight; other quarters skip a fifth reading.

sentences.zh: 其令則隨四時，不以五行為令也，是以服黃無令。

translations.literal: The mandate itself follows the four seasons—it is not keyed to the five phases as a separate command, therefore there is no yellow-season mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal edicts number four, so no standalone “earth” reading exists.

sentences.zh: 」斯則魏氏不讀大暑令也。

translations.literal: ” Thus Wei did not read the great heat mandate.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Wei omitted the great-heat proclamation.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，亦有其制。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate, it too had regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin copied the system.

sentences.zh: 傅咸云：「立秋一日，白路光於紫庭，白旗陳於玉階。

translations.literal: Fu Xian wrote: “On the day of autumn’s establishment, white chariots gleam in the purple court, white banners line the jade steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian described autumn’s first day: white carriages and flags in the palace.

sentences.zh: 」然則其日旗路皆白也。

translations.literal: ” Thus that day’s banners and chariots were all white.
translations.idiomatic: Hence autumn ceremonies favored white equipage.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和五年六月丁未，有司奏讀秋令。

translations.literal: Chengdi, Xianhe 5 sixth month day dingwei, the offices memorialized reading the autumn mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe 5 saw a debate on reciting the autumn command.

sentences.zh: 兼侍中散騎常侍荀奕、兼黃門侍郎散騎侍郎曹宇駁曰：「尚書三公曹奏讀秋令，儀注舊典未備。

translations.literal: Concurrent attendant Xun Yi and concurrent yellow-gate secretary Cao Yu objected: “When the Masters of Writing three-excellencies section memorialized reading the autumn mandate, the ceremonial commentary and old canons were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi and Cao Yu said the handbook lacked detail.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議光祿大夫臣華恆議，武皇帝以秋夏盛暑，常闕不讀令，在春冬不廢也。

translations.literal: We deliberated with Minister of Household Hua Heng’s opinion: Martial Emperor skipped summer and autumn readings because of sweltering heat, but never suspended spring and winter.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Heng recalled Wudi suspending only the hot-season readings.

sentences.zh: 夫先王所以順時讀令者，蓋後天而奉天時，正服尊嚴之所重。

translations.literal: The reason former kings read mandates according to season was to follow heaven after heaven’s time—correct dress is what lends dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings timed proclamations to nature so regalia would awe the court.

sentences.zh: 今服章多闕，加比熱隆赫，臣等謂可如恆議，依故事闕而不讀。

translations.literal: Now court dress is still incomplete, and moreover the heat is fierce; we hold we may follow Heng’s proposal and per precedent omit reading it.
translations.idiomatic: Regalia remains patchy and the weather sweltering; we recommend skipping the summer reading, as Hua Heng urged.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: ” The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，有司奏「今月十六日立夏。

translations.literal: Sixth year third month, the offices memorialized “this month’s sixteenth day is summer’s establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year’s third month officials noted the sixteenth would mark the beginning of summer.

sentences.zh: 今正服漸備，四時讀令，是祗述天和隆殺之道，謂今故宜讀夏令。

translations.literal: Now correct garments are gradually complete; reading the four seasons’ mandates is how we reverently echo heaven’s harmony and waxing and waning—we say that now it is proper to read the summer mandate.
translations.idiomatic: With full ritual dress restored, reciting the summer edict would again align the court with celestial rhythm.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: ” The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request carried.

sentences.zh: 《禮》，孟春之月，「乃擇元辰，天子親載耒耜，措之於參保介之禦間，帥三公九卿諸侯大夫躬耕帝藉」。

translations.literal: The Rites: in the first month of spring “choose a good day; the Son of Heaven personally loads plow and share, sets them between the reins of the team guarding the heir apparent, and leads the three dukes, nine ministers, marquises, and grandees to plow the emperor’s field in person.”
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances tell the king to pick an auspicious day, shoulder the sacred plow, and lead the high nobility through the symbolic furrows of the imperial field.

sentences.zh: 至秦滅學，其禮久廢。

translations.literal: By the time Qin destroyed learning, this rite had long lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin’s war on books killed the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝之後，始行斯典。

translations.literal: After Han Wendi, this canon was first enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han revived it starting with Wendi.

sentences.zh: 魏之三祖，亦皆親耕藉田。

translations.literal: Wei’s three founding emperors all personally plowed the ritual field.
translations.idiomatic: Each of Wei’s three temple emperors worked the sacred acre.

sentences.zh: 及武帝泰始四年，有司奏耕祠先農，可，令有司行事。

translations.literal: When Wudi, Taishi 4, the offices memorialized plowing and sacrificing to First Farmer—approved—ordering the offices to conduct the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 4 officials asked to combine plowing with First Farmer worship; the emperor agreed to delegate the liturgy.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫國之大事，在祀與農。

translations.literal: Edict: “The great affairs of state are sacrifice and agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that worship and farming anchor the realm.

sentences.zh: 是以古之聖王，躬耕帝藉，以供郊廟之粢盛，且以訓化天下。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient sage-kings personally plowed the emperor’s field to supply grain for suburban and temple offerings, and thereby instructed and transformed all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Sage-kings hoed the imperial plot so temple grain would be pure and so peasants would take their cue from the throne.

sentences.zh: 近世以來，耕藉止于數步之中，空有慕古之名，曾無供祀訓農之實，而有百官車徒之費。

translations.literal: In recent generations plowing the field has stopped within a few paces—empty reputation for antiquity, no real supply for sacrifice or lesson for farmers, yet with the expense of a hundred officials’ chariots and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the “plowing” shrank to a few steps—a hollow antique show that fed no altars and taught no one, while processions still cost a fortune.

sentences.zh: 今修千畝之制，當與群公卿士躬稼穡之艱難，以率先天下。

translations.literal: Now restoring the thousand-mu system, we ought with dukes and ministers personally to endure the hardship of hoeing and harrowing, to lead the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Reviving the thousand-mu field means sharing the sweat of real tillage with the nobility to set an example.

sentences.zh: 主者詳具其制，下河南，處田地于東郊之南，洛水之北。

translations.literal: Let the responsible office detail the regulations, transmit them to Henan, and locate the land south of the eastern suburb and north of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus were told to lay out plots east of the capital above the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 若無官田，隨宜使換，而不得侵人也。

translations.literal: If there is no government field, exchange land as suitable, but do not encroach on private holdings.
translations.idiomatic: Where no public acre existed, officials might swap plots but never seize private soil.

sentences.zh: 」於是乘輿禦木輅以耕，乙太牢祀先農。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the imperial carriage drove a wooden chariot to plow and sacrificed to First Farmer with a tai-lao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode a plain wood cart through the furrows and offered a full tai-lao to First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 自惠帝之後，其事便廢。

translations.literal: From Huidi onward the matter was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After Huidi the rite died out again.

sentences.zh: 江左元帝將修耕藉，尚書符問「藉田至尊應躬祠先農不」？

translations.literal: When Yuan-di on the left bank of the river was about to restore plowing, the Masters of Writing dispatch asked “for the ritual field ought the sovereign personally sacrifice to First Farmer or not?”
translations.idiomatic: As eastern Jin planned the ceremony, the ministry asked whether the emperor must officiate at First Farmer himself.

sentences.zh: 賀循答：「漢儀無，止有至尊應自祭之文。

translations.literal: He Xun replied: “Han observance lacks explicit text—only wording that the sovereign ought to sacrifice in person.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun answered that Han codes implied personal attendance without spelling out every step.

sentences.zh: 然則《周禮》王者祭四望則毳冕，祭社稷五祀則絺冕，以此不為無親祭之義也。

translations.literal: Yet the Rites of Zhou: when the king sacrifices to the four wang he wears a feathered robe; when sacrificing to soil gods and five household spirits he wears fine linen—this shows personal sacrifice is not excluded.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou canon still lists distinct crowns for personal cults to land and hearth spirits.

sentences.zh: 宜立兩儀注。

translations.literal: It is fitting to draw up paired ceremonial commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed drafting parallel handbooks for the two questions.

sentences.zh: 」賀循等所上儀注又未詳允，事竟不行。

translations.literal: ” The ceremonial drafts He Xun and others submitted were still not detailed enough, and the affair in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Their handbook proved too thin and the plan stalled.

sentences.zh: 後哀帝復欲行其典，亦不能遂。

translations.literal: Later Aidi wished again to enact the canon, yet could not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Aidi’s later attempt likewise failed.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，縣邑常以乙未日祠先農，乃耕於乙地，以丙戌日祠風伯于戌地，以已醜日祠雨師於醜地，牲用羊豕。

translations.literal: Han observance: districts and towns regularly on yiwei day sacrificed to First Farmer, then plowed on yi earth; on bingxu day sacrificed to the wind elder on xu ground; on jichou day sacrificed to the rain master on chou ground—victims were sheep and swine.
translations.idiomatic: Local Han calendars tied First Farmer, wind, and rain offerings to stem-branch days with sheep or pigs.

sentences.zh: 立春之日，皆青幡幘迎春於東郊外野中。

translations.literal: On the day spring is established, all used green pennants and headcloths to welcome spring east of the suburb in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Spring’s first day brought green banners to the eastern outskirts.

sentences.zh: 迎春至自野中出，則迎拜之而還，弗祭。

translations.literal: When the spring welcome returned from the wilds, they bowed in greeting and came back—they did not sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers saluted the returning spring heralds without an altar service.

sentences.zh: 三時不迎。

translations.literal: The other three seasons had no welcoming procession.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, autumn, and winter held no such parade.

sentences.zh: 魏氏雖天子耕藉，籓鎮闕諸侯百畝之禮。

translations.literal: Although Wei’s Son of Heaven plowed the ritual field, fiefs lacked the marquis’s hundred-mu observance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s emperors hoed, but princely domains skipped the classical hundred-mu lesson.

sentences.zh: 及武帝末，有司奏：「古諸侯耕藉田百畝，躬執耒以奉社稷宗廟，以勸率農功。

translations.literal: When Wudi neared his end, the offices memorialized: “Anciently marquises plowed a hundred mu of ritual field, personally wielding the plow to supply the altars of soil and grain and ancestral shrines, thereby encouraging farming.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wudi’s reign ministers cited the feudal hundred-mu rule meant to feed state altars and teach husbandry.

sentences.zh: 今諸王臨國，宜依修耕藉之義。

translations.literal: Now princes holding their states ought to restore plowing’s meaning.
translations.idiomatic: They urged each enfeoffed prince to copy the rite.

sentences.zh: 」然竟未施行。

translations.literal: ” Yet in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，王后帥內外命婦享先蠶於北郊。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: the queen leads inner and outer titled women to feast the First Silkworm north of the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou law placed the queen’s silkworm cult north of the city.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，皇后親桑東郊苑中，蠶室祭蠶神，曰苑窳婦人、寓氏公主，祠用少牢。

translations.literal: Han observance: the empress personally tended mulberry in the eastern park; the silkworm chamber sacrificed to the silkworm spirits called the Park Grotto Woman and Princess Yu-shi, using a shao-lao.
translations.idiomatic: Han empresses fed silkworms east of the capital and offered a pig-and-sheep pair to tutelary silk spirits.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初七年正月，命中宮蠶於北郊，依周典也。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu 7 first month, ordered the inner palace to raise silkworms north of the suburb, following Zhou’s canon.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi moved the harem rite to the northern field in Huangchu 7 to match Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及武帝太康六年，散騎常侍華嶠奏：「先王之制，天子諸侯親耕藉田千畝，後夫人躬蠶桑。

translations.literal: When Wudi, Taikang 6, cavalier attendant Hua Jiao memorialized: “Ancient institutions had Son of Heaven and marquises personally plow a thousand mu of ritual field, and the empress and consorts personally tend mulberry and silkworm.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 6 Hua Jiao reminded the court that kings and queens once shared the plow and the silkworm tray.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以聖明至仁，修先王之緒，皇后體資生之德，合配乾之義，而坤道未光，蠶禮尚缺。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty with sagely clarity and supreme benevolence continues the work of former kings; the empress embodies the virtue that nurtures life and matches the meaning of heaven’s complement—yet the way of earth is not yet radiant and the silkworm rite still lacks.
translations.idiomatic: He praised the emperor’s virtue and noted the empress still lacked a public silk ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以為宜依古式，備斯盛典。

translations.literal: We hold it fitting to follow ancient forms and complete this great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a full classical observance.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「昔天子親藉，以供粢盛，後夫人躬蠶，以備祭服，所以聿遵孝敬，明教示訓也。

translations.literal: ” Edict: “Formerly the Son of Heaven personally plowed to supply grain offerings, and the empress personally tended silkworms to supply sacrificial robes—thereby earnestly honoring filial devotion and clarifying instruction by example.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered that grain and silk from royal hands once proved filial care and moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 今藉田有制，而蠶禮不修，由中間務多，未暇崇備。

translations.literal: Now the ritual field has regulations, yet the silkworm rite is not cultivated—because mid-course there were many tasks and no leisure to exalt completeness.
