translations.idiomatic: Plowing had rules; silk rites lapsed amid busy government.

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，宜修禮以示四海。

translations.literal: Now the realm is without incident; it is fitting to repair ritual to show the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Peace allowed the court to finish what war had postponed.

sentences.zh: 其詳依古典，及近代故事，以參今宜，明年施行。

translations.literal: Let it be detailed according to classical antiquity and recent precedents, consulting present suitability, to be enacted next year.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should blend old texts with recent examples for adoption the following year.

sentences.zh: 」於是蠶於西郊，蓋與藉田對其方也。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they raised silkworms west of the suburb, pairing that direction with the ritual field.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworms moved to the western field to balance the eastern plow plot.

sentences.zh: 乃使侍中成粲草定其儀。

translations.literal: They ordered attendant Cheng Can to draft the observance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Can wrote the liturgy.

sentences.zh: 先蠶壇高一丈，方二丈，為四出陛，陛廣五尺，在皇后采桑壇東南帷宮外門之外，而東南去帷宮十丈，在蠶室西南，桑林在其東。

translations.literal: The First Silkworm altar was one zhang high, two zhang square, with four stepped approaches five chi wide, outside the southeast gate of the curtained palace beyond the empress’s mulberry altar—ten zhang southeast of the curtain palace, southwest of the silkworm chamber, mulberry grove east of it.
translations.idiomatic: They built a square mound with ramps beside the queen’s temporary palace and silkworm house.

sentences.zh: 取列侯妻六人為蠶母。

translations.literal: They took six wives of full marquises as silkworm matrons.
translations.idiomatic: Six noblewives supervised the trays.

sentences.zh: 蠶將生，擇吉日，皇后著十二笄步搖，依漢魏故事，衣青衣，乘油畫雲母安車，駕六騩馬。

translations.literal: When the silkworms were about to hatch, on an auspicious day the empress wore twelve hairpins and swaying step-tassels, following Han-Wei precedent, green robes, riding an oil-painted mica carriage drawn by six dappled horses.
translations.idiomatic: On hatching day she dressed in green with Han-style regalia and rode a decorated six-horse coach.

sentences.zh: 女尚書著貂蟬佩璽陪乘，載筐鉤。

translations.literal: Female secretaries in sable-tasseled caps and seal pendants accompanied, carrying baskets and hooks.
translations.idiomatic: Female scribes in formal pins rode along with harvest baskets.

sentences.zh: 公主、三夫人、九嬪、世婦、諸太妃、太夫人及縣鄉君、郡公侯特進夫人、外世婦、命婦皆步搖、衣青，各載筐鉤從蠶。

translations.literal: Princesses, the three senior consorts, the nine concubines, palace matrons, imperial concubines of rank, grandees’ wives, district and village mistresses, ducal and marquis ladies of special advance, outer palace matrons, and titled women all wore swaying tassels and green, each with basket and hook, following the silkworm procession.
translations.idiomatic: The whole female nobility trailed in green with picking gear.

sentences.zh: 先桑二日，蠶室生蠶著薄上。

translations.literal: Two days before mulberry-picking, the silkworm chamber hatched worms onto trays.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-eight hours ahead, attendants spread newly hatched worms on mats.

sentences.zh: 桑日，皇后未到，太祝令質明以一太牢告祠，謁者一人監祠。

translations.literal: On mulberry day, before the empress arrived, the grand invocator at dawn sacrificed one tai-lao with announcement, one usher supervising the cult.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a tai-lao announced the rite before the queen appeared.

sentences.zh: 祠畢撤饌，班余胙于從桑及奉祠者。

translations.literal: When sacrifice ended they cleared the offerings and distributed leftover meat to mulberry followers and cult attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Leftover sacrificial meat went to helpers.

sentences.zh: 皇后至西郊升壇，公主以下陪列壇東。

translations.literal: The empress reached the western suburb, ascended the altar; princesses and below lined east of the mound.
translations.idiomatic: She mounted the western terrace with noblewomen ranked to her east.

sentences.zh: 皇后東面躬桑，采三條，諸妃公主各采五條，縣鄉君以下各采九條，悉以桑授蠶母，還蠶室。

translations.literal: The empress faced east, personally picked mulberry—three branches; consorts and princesses five each; district and village ladies nine each—all handed the leaves to silkworm matrons and returned to the silkworm chamber.
translations.idiomatic: She took three sprays; higher-ranking women five; lower ranks nine; matrons fed the worms.

sentences.zh: 事訖，皇后還便坐，公主以下乃就位，設饗宴，賜絹各有差。

translations.literal: When finished, the empress withdrew to an informal seat; only then did princesses and below take places, a feast was spread, and silk gifts were granted in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they feasted and distributed silk by rank.

sentences.zh: 前漢但置官社而無官稷，王莽置官稷，後復省。

translations.literal: Former Han set only an official soil altar, no official grain altar; Wang Mang added an official grain altar, later abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han lacked a state grain shrine until Wang Mang, who later removed it.

sentences.zh: 故漢至魏但太社有稷，而官社無稷，故常二社一稷也。

translations.literal: Thus from Han through Wei only the Grand Altar of Soil included grain, while the official soil altar lacked grain—hence normally two soil altars and one grain.
translations.idiomatic: The usual layout was twin soil shrines sharing a single grain god.

sentences.zh: 晉初仍魏，無所增損。

translations.literal: Early Jin continued Wei without addition or subtraction.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin copied Wei’s arrangement intact.

sentences.zh: 至太康九年，改建宗廟，而社稷壇一廟俱徙。

translations.literal: By Taikang 9 they rebuilt the ancestral temple and moved both the soil-and-grain mound and one temple together.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 9’s temple project shifted the twin altars.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「社實一神，其並二社之祀。

translations.literal: An edict then said: “Soil is in truth one spirit; merge the cult of the twin soil altars.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proposed unifying the duplicated soil worship.

sentences.zh: 」於是車騎司馬傅咸表曰：

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Cavalry Commandant Fu Xian submitted:
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian answered with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 《祭法》王社太社，各有其義。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifices’ king’s soil and grand soil each has its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Sacrifice distinguishes royal field-altar from national altar.

sentences.zh: 天子尊事郊廟，故冕而躬耕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven reverently serves suburban and temple shrines, hence wears full crown and plows in person.
translations.idiomatic: The king dons regalia for heaven and ancestors, then takes the plow.

sentences.zh: 躬耕也者，所以重孝享之粢盛。

translations.literal: Personal plowing is the means by which one esteems the grain for filial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The furrow ritual supplies pure grain for ancestral vessels.

sentences.zh: 親耕故自報，自為立社者，為藉田而報者也。

translations.literal: Because of personal plowing he reports for himself; establishing a soil altar for oneself is reporting for the ritual field.
translations.idiomatic: The private royal altar thanks the soil that feeds the sacred acre.

sentences.zh: 國以人為本，人以穀為命，故又為百姓立社而祈報焉。

translations.literal: The state takes people as root, people take grain as life—hence he also establishes a soil altar for the hundred surnames and prays in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: A second altar speaks for common farmers.

sentences.zh: 事異報殊，此社之所以有二也。

translations.literal: Affairs differ and reports differ—this is why there are two altars.
translations.idiomatic: Two purposes require two mounds.

sentences.zh: 王景侯之論王社，亦謂春祈藉田，秋而報之也。

translations.literal: Wang Jinghou’s discussion of the king’s soil also says spring prayer for the ritual field and autumn thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su tied the royal altar to spring petitions and autumn repayment.

sentences.zh: 其論太社，則曰王者布下圻內，為百姓立之，謂之大社，不自立之於京都也。

translations.literal: His discussion of grand soil says the king spreads it within his domain for the hundred surnames—it is called grand soil; he does not establish it only in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang called the national altar a realm-wide shrine for subjects, not a capital-only cult.

sentences.zh: 景侯此論據《祭法》。

translations.literal: Jinghou’s thesis cites the Record of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su quoted the Canon of Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《祭法》：「大夫以下成群立社，曰置社。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifices: “Below grandee rank, groups establish soil altars—called ‘placed altars.’
translations.idiomatic: The text allows local “placed” village shrines.

sentences.zh: 」景侯解曰，「今之里社是也」。

translations.literal: ” Jinghou explains, “Today’s village altars are these.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang equated them with modern hamlet shrines.

sentences.zh: 景侯解《祭法》，則以置社為人間之社矣。

translations.literal: Jinghou’s gloss on the Record of Sacrifices thus treats placed altars as human-world shrines.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary keeps village cults separate from state cults.

sentences.zh: 而別論復乙太社為人間之社，未曉此旨也。

translations.literal: Yet in another argument he again treats grand soil as a human-world shrine—this misses the point.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere Wang blurred the national altar into a mere local shrine—incoherent.

sentences.zh: 太社，天子為百姓而祀，故稱天子社。

translations.literal: Grand soil: the Son of Heaven sacrifices for the hundred surnames—hence it is called the Son of Heaven’s soil.
translations.idiomatic: The great altar serves all subjects under the king’s charge.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》曰：「天子太社，必受霜露風雨。

translations.literal: The Summons of the Single Victim says: “The Son of Heaven’s grand soil must receive frost, dew, wind, and rain.
translations.idiomatic: A suburban scripture insists the national altar stand open to sky.

sentences.zh: 」以群姓之眾，王者通為立社，故稱太社也。

translations.literal: ” Because the multitude of clans is vast, the king universally establishes this altar for them—hence it is called grand soil.
translations.idiomatic: Open-air placement shows it belongs to everyone.

sentences.zh: 若夫置社，其數不一，蓋以裏所為名，《左氏傳》盟於清丘之社是也。

translations.literal: As for placed altars, their number is not fixed—they take hamlet names, as when the Zuo Commentary tells of covenant at Qingqiu’s altar.
translations.idiomatic: Local shrines multiply under place names like Qingqiu.

sentences.zh: 眾庶之社，既已不稱太矣，若復不立之京都，當安所立乎！

translations.literal: Commoners’ altars already are not called “grand”; if they are not set in the capital, where should they stand!
translations.idiomatic: Village earth gods cannot replace the capital’s national mound.

sentences.zh: 《祭法》又曰，王為群姓立七祀，王自為立七祀。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifices also says the king establishes seven household spirits for the clans and seven for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The same canon lists seven domestic spirits for the people and seven personal to the king.

sentences.zh: 言自為者，自為而祀也；

translations.literal: “For himself” means he sacrifices for himself;
translations.idiomatic: Personal cults serve the royal house alone.

sentences.zh: 為群姓者，為群姓而祀也。

translations.literal: “For the clans” means he sacrifices for the clans.
translations.idiomatic: Public cults embrace all subjects.

sentences.zh: 太社與七祀其文正等。

translations.literal: Grand soil and the seven spirits share parallel wording.
translations.idiomatic: The grammar matches royal versus national rites.

sentences.zh: 說者窮此，因雲墳籍但有五祀，無七祀也。

translations.literal: Commentators exhaust this point and therefore say texts preserve only five spirits, not seven.
translations.idiomatic: Some scholars collapse seven into five by sleight of hand.

sentences.zh: 案祭，五祀國之大祀，七者小祀。

translations.literal: Examining sacrifice: the five spirits are great state cults; the seven are lesser cults.
translations.idiomatic: Five are major; seven are minor domestic offerings.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》所雲祭凡小祀，則墨冕之屬也。

translations.literal: What the Rites of Zhou calls “all lesser sacrifices” belongs to ink-crown rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou labels them secondary, ink-crowned services.

sentences.zh: 景侯解大厲曰，「如周杜伯，鬼有所歸，乃不為厲」。

translations.literal: Jinghou glosses great plague-spirit as “like Zhou’s Earl Du—when a ghost has a home it ceases to plague.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su explained plague gods as wronged spirits given rest.

sentences.zh: 今雲無二社者稱景侯，《祭法》不謂無二，則曰「口傳無其文也」。

translations.literal: Now those who say there should not be two altars cite Jinghou; the Record of Sacrifices does not say there are not two, yet they claim “oral teaching lacks the text.”
translations.idiomatic: Dual-altar skeptics quote Wang Su yet ignore explicit classical lines.

sentences.zh: 夫以景侯之明，擬議而後為解，而欲以口論除明文，如此非但二社當見思惟，景侯之後解亦未易除也。

translations.literal: Given Jinghou’s brilliance, deliberating before explaining—yet wishing to erase clear writing by chatter—not only should the two-altar question be rethought, Jinghou’s later glosses are not easily dismissed either.
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Su’s word can overthrow scripture, nothing in his corpus is safe either.

sentences.zh: 前被敕，《尚書·召告》乃社於新邑，惟一太牢，不二社之明義也。

translations.literal: Earlier I received order: the Documents’ “Shao Gao” sets up soil at the new city with only one tai-lao—clear meaning there are not two altars.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang founding chapter offered one bull at a single altar—strong evidence against duplication.

sentences.zh: 案《郊特牲》曰社稷太牢，必援一牢之文以明社之無二，則稷無牲矣。

translations.literal: Examining the Summons of the Single Victim, soil and grain use tai-lao—if one insists on one victim to prove a single altar, then grain has no victim.
translations.idiomatic: Literalists who cite one bull forget grain needs its own offering.

sentences.zh: 說者曰，舉社則稷可知。

translations.literal: Commentators say naming soil implies grain.
translations.idiomatic: Traditional gloss: mention earth, millet follows.

sentences.zh: 苟可舉社以明稷，何獨不舉一以明二？

translations.literal: If soil can stand for grain, why cannot one altar stand for two?
translations.idiomatic: If synecdoche works for grain, it can defend twin altars too.

sentences.zh: 國之大事，在祀與戎。

translations.literal: The great affairs of state are sacrifice and war.
translations.idiomatic: Statecraft rests on altars and armies.

sentences.zh: 若有二而除之，不若過而存之。

translations.literal: If there are two and you remove them, it is not as good as erring on the side of keeping them.
translations.idiomatic: Better a redundant mound than a rash demolition.

sentences.zh: 況存之有義，而除之無據乎？

translations.literal: Moreover keeping them has principle; removing them lacks warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition supports preservation; merger lacks proof.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》封人掌設社壝，無稷字。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou’s border officer sets up soil dikes—there is no “grain” character.
translations.idiomatic: The border-warden passage in the Rites of Zhou speaks only of earthworks around the soil altar, never the word grain.

sentences.zh: 今帝社無稷，蓋出於此。

translations.literal: Now the emperor’s soil altar lacks grain—probably for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: The royal field-altar omits grain icons following that passage.

sentences.zh: 然國主社稷，故經傳動稱社稷。

translations.literal: Yet the state masters soil and grain—hence classics always say “soil-and-grain” together.
translations.idiomatic: Still, idiom pairs earth and millet as the realm’s twin pillars.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》王祭社稷則絺冕，此王社有稷之交也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: when the king sacrifices to soil and grain he wears fine linen—this is the text showing the king’s soil includes grain.
translations.idiomatic: The king’s linen crown for the combined cult proves his altar honors both earth and crops.

sentences.zh: 封人所掌社壝之無稷字，說者以為略文，從可知也。

translations.literal: Commentators hold that the border officer’s charge of soil dikes lacking the word “grain” is abbreviated wording—from it grain may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars treat the missing “grain” as shorthand; millet is still implied.

sentences.zh: 謂宜仍舊立二社，而加立帝社之稷。

translations.literal: We say it is fitting to keep the old establishment of two soil altars and additionally add grain to the emperor’s soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian urged keeping twin earth shrines while adding a grain seat to the royal field-altar.

sentences.zh: 時成粲義稱景侯論太社不立京都，欲破鄭氏學。

translations.literal: At the time Cheng Can’s argument cited Jinghou’s thesis that grand soil is not set in the capital, intending to break Zheng Xuan’s school.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Can used Wang Su to attack Zheng’s reading of the national altar.

sentences.zh: 咸重表以為：「如粲之論，景侯之解文以此壞。

translations.literal: All Xian again memorialized: “According to Can’s argument, Jinghou’s textual gloss is thereby broken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian replied that Cheng’s logic undoes Wang Su’s own commentary.

sentences.zh: 《大雅》雲'乃立塚土'，毛公解曰，'塚土，大社也。

translations.literal: The Great Odes says ‘then he raised the mound of earth’; Mao’s gloss says ‘mound of earth is grand soil.’
translations.idiomatic: The Mao commentary equates the “great mound” with the state altar.

sentences.zh: '景侯解《詩》，即用此說。

translations.literal: ” Jinghou glossing the Odes employs this explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su’s reading of the poem depends on that equation.

sentences.zh: 《禹貢》'惟土五色'，景侯解曰，'王者取五色土為太社，封四方諸侯，各割其方色土者覆四方也'。

translations.literal: The Tribute of Yu says ‘only earth of five colors’; Jinghou glosses, ‘The king takes five-colored earth for grand soil, enfeoffs the four-direction marquises, each cutting his direction’s colored earth to cover the four quarters.’
translations.idiomatic: Wang also read the Yu document as mandating five-colored clods at the capital for enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 如此，太社復為立京都也。

translations.literal: In this way grand soil again means establishing it in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That reading puts the grand altar squarely in the capital after all.

sentences.zh: 不知此論何從而出，而與解乖，上違經記明文，下壞景侯之解。

translations.literal: I do not know whence this thesis emerged—it clashes with the gloss, violates clear classical wording above, and breaks Jinghou’s solution below.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian called Cheng’s view incoherent with Wang’s own exegesis.

sentences.zh: 臣雖頑蔽，少長學門，不能默已，謹復續上。

translations.literal: Though I am dull, having grown in the school gate I cannot stay silent and respectfully continue my submission.
translations.idiomatic: He protested despite modesty.

sentences.zh: 」劉寔與咸議同。

translations.literal: ” Liu Shi agreed with Xian’s opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi sided with Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「社實一神，而相襲二位，眾議不同，何必改作！

translations.literal: Edict: “Soil is truly one spirit, yet we inherit two positions—opinions differ—why must we reform!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused merger: one god might sit under two names.

sentences.zh: 其便仍舊，一如魏制。」

translations.literal: Let it remain as before, entirely like Wei regulations.”
translations.idiomatic: The court kept Wei’s twin-altar layout.

sentences.zh: 其後摯虞奏，以為：「臣案《祭法》'王為群姓立社曰太社，王自'為立社曰王社。

translations.literal: Later Zhi Yu memorialized, holding: “Examining the Record of Sacrifices, ‘The king establishes soil for the clans—called grand soil; the king establishes soil for himself—called king’s soil.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu reopened the debate with the Canon of Sacrifice’s paired definitions.

sentences.zh: '《周禮》大司徒'設其社稷之壝'，又曰'以血祭祭社稷'，則太社也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou’s grand minister of education ‘sets the dikes of its soil and grain,’ and also says ‘with blood sacrifice sacrifice to soil and grain’—that is grand soil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s minister of lands rings both earth and millet— the national cult.

sentences.zh: 又曰'封人掌設王之社壝'，又有軍旅宜乎社，則王社也。

translations.literal: It also says ‘the border officer sets up the king’s soil dikes,’ and again when there is army campaign there is appropriate sacrifice at soil—that is king’s soil.
translations.idiomatic: The royal furrow-altar appears in the border officer and military clauses.

sentences.zh: 太社為群姓祈報，祈報有時，主不可廢。

translations.literal: Grand soil prays and thanks for the clans; prayer and thanks have seasons—the chief cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The public altar’s seasonal reports cannot lapse.

sentences.zh: 故凡祓社釁鼓，主奉以從是也。

translations.literal: Hence whenever one purifies soil or smears blood on drums, the chief tablet accompanies—that is the case.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign rites carry the earth god’s tablet for a reason.

sentences.zh: 此皆二社之明文，前代之所尊。

translations.literal: These are all clear texts on the two altars, honored by former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Classics and history both respect the pairing.

sentences.zh: 以《尚書·召告》社於新邑三牲各文，《詩》稱'乃立塚土'，無兩社之交，故廢帝社，惟立太社。

translations.literal: Because the Documents’ ‘Shao Gao’ sets up soil at the new city with separate wording for three victims, and the Odes says ‘then he raised the mound of earth,’ with no text on two altars, they abolished the emperor’s soil and kept only grand soil.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier reformers cited Shang founding lines to justify cutting the royal altar.

sentences.zh: 《詩書》所稱，各指一事，又皆在公旦製作之前，未可以易《周禮》之明典，《祭法》之正義。

translations.literal: What the Documents and Odes cite each refers to one affair, and all lie before the Duke of Zhou’s compilation—one may not use them to change the Rites of Zhou’s clear canon and the Record of Sacrifices’ correct meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu warned against letting pre-Zhou fragments overturn Zhou and ritual-canon law.

sentences.zh: 前改建廟社，營一社之處，朝議斐然，執古匡今。

translations.literal: Earlier, rebuilding temple and soil, locating one altar’s site, court debate flourished, clutching antiquity to correct the present.
translations.idiomatic: The Taikang move had already sparked controversy.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝躬發明詔，定二社之義，以為永制。

translations.literal: Shizu Martial Emperor personally issued an edict clarifying the meaning of two altars, taking it as perpetual regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had fixed the dual-altar doctrine for all time.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，從二社。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the new ritual following the two altars.
translations.idiomatic: The code should codify both mounds again.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ” The edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted Zhi Yu.

sentences.zh: 至元帝建武元年，又依洛京立二社一稷。

translations.literal: By Yuandi’s Jianwu 1 they again followed Luoyang in setting two altars and one grain.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin’s first year mirrored Luoyang: two earths, one millet.

sentences.zh: 其太社之祝曰：「地德普施，惠存無疆。

translations.literal: The grand soil prayer said: “Earth’s virtue spreads broadly, its favor endures without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The national altar’s hymn praised earth’s universal bounty.

sentences.zh: 乃建太社，保佑萬邦。

translations.literal: Thereupon we establish grand soil, guarding and blessing the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: They raised the altar to shield all states.

sentences.zh: 悠悠四海，咸賴嘉祥。

translations.literal: Far stretches the four seas—all rely on auspicious blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The poem called the realm to trust the gift of soil.

sentences.zh: 」其帝社之祝曰：「坤德厚載，邦畿是保。

translations.literal: ” The emperor’s soil prayer said: “The way of earth bears thickly, the capital domain thereby is protected.
translations.idiomatic: The royal field-altar hymn stressed the capital’s bond with chthonic power.

sentences.zh: 乃建帝社，以神地道。

translations.literal: Thereupon we establish emperor’s soil, thereby spiritizing the way of earth.
translations.idiomatic: They framed it as making the soil cult numinous.

sentences.zh: 明祀惟辰，景福來造。」

translations.literal: Bright sacrifice chooses the season; great blessing comes to visit.”
translations.idiomatic: Timed worship would draw fortune down.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，每月旦，太史上其月曆，有司侍郎尚書見讀其令，奉行其正。

translations.literal: Han observance: each new moon’s first day the grand astrologer presented the monthly calendar; the relevant vice director and masters of writing met, read the mandate, and enacted its corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Han began each month with astrologers delivering the calendar and ministers reading commands.

sentences.zh: 朔前後二日，牽牛酒至社下以祭日。

translations.literal: On the two days before and after new moon they led oxen and wine below the soil altar to sacrifice to the sun.
translations.idiomatic: They greeted the solar node at the earth shrine with libations.

sentences.zh: 日有變，割羊以祠社，用救日變。

translations.literal: If the sun showed anomaly, they cut a sheep to sacrifice to soil, using it to rescue a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipses triggered sheep offerings at the altar of earth.

sentences.zh: 執事者長冠，衣絳領袖緣中衣、絳緣以行禮，如故事。

translations.literal: Officiants wore tall caps, inner garments with crimson collars and cuffs edged crimson, crimson borders, performing the rite as in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Participants dressed in prescribed crimson-trimmed robes.

sentences.zh: 自晉受命，日月將交會，太史乃上合朔，尚書先事三日，宣攝內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: From Jin receiving the mandate, whenever sun and moon would meet in conjunction, the grand astrologer reported the expected new moon; the masters of writing three days beforehand proclaimed full vigilance inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Jin required three days’ martial alert before predicted conjunctions.

sentences.zh: 摯虞《決疑》曰：「凡救日蝕者，著赤幘，以助陽也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu’s Resolving Doubts says: “All who rescue solar eclipse wear red headcloths to assist yang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu prescribed red kerchiefs to strengthen the sun’s fire.

sentences.zh: 日將蝕，天子素服避正殿，內外嚴警。

translations.literal: As eclipse nears, the Son of Heaven in plain garb avoids the main hall; inside and outside are strictly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign withdrew to undyed robes while the palace locked down.

sentences.zh: 太史登靈台，伺侯日變，便伐鼓於門。

translations.literal: The grand astrologer mounts the spirit terrace, watches for solar change, then beats drums at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Observers on the tower triggered gate drums at first bite.

sentences.zh: 聞鼓音，侍臣皆著赤幘，帶劍入侍。

translations.literal: Hearing the drum, attending ministers all don red kerchiefs, gird swords, and enter attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers armed themselves in red caps when drums sounded.

sentences.zh: 三台令史以上皆各持劍，立其戶前。

translations.literal: Secretaries of the three platforms and above each grasped a sword, standing before their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Every senior scribe stood sword in hand at his office.

sentences.zh: 衛尉卿驅馳繞宮，伺察守備。

translations.literal: The commandant of the guard galloped circuits around the palace, inspecting readiness.
translations.idiomatic: The captain of the guard rode patrols to check defenses.

sentences.zh: 周而復始，亦伐鼓於社，用周禮也。

translations.literal: Round and round they also beat drums at soil, using Zhou rite.
translations.idiomatic: Community altars echoed the drums per Zhou law.

sentences.zh: 又以赤絲為繩以系社，祝史陳辭以責之。

translations.literal: They also used red silk rope to bind the soil altar; invocators spread phrases to reproach it.
translations.idiomatic: Red cords lashed the earth god while priests scolded him.

sentences.zh: 社，勾龍之神，天子之上公，故陳辭以責之。

translations.literal: Soil is the spirit of Goulong, the Son of Heaven’s senior duke—hence phrases reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: The earth deity ranked as a lord deserving rebuke when heaven misbehaved.

sentences.zh: 日復常，乃罷。」

translations.literal: When the sun returned to normal, then they stopped.”
translations.idiomatic: Rites ended once daylight recovered.

sentences.zh: 漢建安中，將正會，而太史上言，正旦當日蝕。

translations.literal: Han Jian’an era, about to hold the new-year court assembly, the grand astrologer reported new year’s dawn would see solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han astrologers predicted a New Year eclipse.

sentences.zh: 朝士疑會否，共諮尚書令荀彧。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen doubted whether to convene and jointly consulted Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers asked Xun Yu whether to cancel court.

sentences.zh: 時廣平計吏劉邵在坐，曰：「梓慎、裨灶，古之良史，尤占水火，錯失天時。

translations.literal: At the time Guangping clerk Liu Shao was present and said: “Zishen and Pizao were fine ancient astrologers, yet even in divining water and fire they missed heaven’s timing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao noted even legendary clerks erred in forecasting.

sentences.zh: 《禮》，諸侯旅見天子，入門不得終禮者四，日蝕在一。

translations.literal: The Rites: when feudal lords travel-audience the Son of Heaven, there are four cases where entering the gate they cannot finish the rite—solar eclipse is one.
translations.idiomatic: Canon lists eclipse among rites that halt mid-ceremony.

sentences.zh: 然則聖人垂制，不為變異豫廢朝禮者，或災消異伏，或推術謬誤也。

translations.literal: Yet sages handed down regulation not to cancel court rites in advance because of anomalies—either the portent vanishes or calculation errs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu argued sages refused to scrap court on a forecast alone.

sentences.zh: 」彧及眾人咸善而從之，遂朝會如舊，日亦不蝕，邵由此顯名。

translations.literal: ” Yu and the crowd approved and followed; they held court assembly as usual—the sun was not eclipsed—and Shao thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: The court met; no eclipse came; Liu Shao won renown.

sentences.zh: 至康帝建元元年，太史上元日合朔，後復疑應卻會與否。

translations.literal: By Kangdi, Jianyuan 1, the grand astrologer reported new year’s day conjunction; again they doubted whether to postpone assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin faced the same New Year eclipse question.

sentences.zh: 庾冰輔政，寫劉邵議以示八坐。

translations.literal: Yu Bing as regent copied Liu Shao’s argument to show the eight seats.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing circulated Liu’s memo.

sentences.zh: 于時有謂邵為不得禮意，荀彧從之，是勝人之一失。

translations.literal: Some then said Shao missed ritual meaning, that Yu’s assent was one instance of overruling others.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called the precedent a mistake.

sentences.zh: 故蔡謨遂著議非之，曰：「邵論災消異伏，又以梓慎、裨灶猶有錯失，太史上言，亦不必審，其理誠然也。

translations.literal: Hence Cai Mo then wrote a critique: “Shao’s point that portents may vanish and that Zishen and Pizao still erred, and that grand astrologers’ reports need not be exact—the principle is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Cai conceded forecasters could be wrong.

sentences.zh: 而雲聖人垂制，不為變異豫廢朝禮，此則謬矣。

translations.literal: Yet to say sages’ institutions do not cancel court in advance over anomalies—this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: But claiming sages ignored omens misreads the canon.

sentences.zh: 災祥之發，所以譴告人君，王者之所重誡，故素服廢樂，退避正寢，百官降物，用幣伐鼓，躬親而救之。

translations.literal: When auspicious and ominous signs appear it is to warn the lord of men; kings greatly heed such admonition—hence plain garments, music stopped, withdrawal from the main chamber, hundred officials lowering regalia, using silks, beating drums, personally hastening to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s warnings demand austerity, drums, and personal penance.

sentences.zh: 夫敬誡之事，與其疑而廢之，寧慎而行之。

translations.literal: In matters of reverent fear, better cautiously perform them than doubt and abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Piety prefers excess to negligence.

sentences.zh: 故孔子、老聃助葬於巷黨，以喪不見星而行，故日蝕而止柩，曰安知其不見星也。

translations.literal: Hence Confucius and Laozi assisted a burial in Lane Party—because funerals may not travel under starlight, when eclipse came they halted the bier, saying “How do we know we will not lack starlight?”
translations.idiomatic: Sages once stopped a funeral cortège for an eclipse—uncertainty justified pause.

sentences.zh: 而邵廢之，是棄聖賢之成規也。

translations.literal: Yet Shao abolished that—this discards the settled rule of sages worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu’s policy ignored that example.

sentences.zh: 魯桓公壬申有災，而以乙亥嘗祭，《春秋》譏之。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Lu on renshen had disaster, yet on yihai held the autumn chang sacrifice—the Spring and Autumn censures it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huan’s mistimed sacrifice drew canonical blame.

sentences.zh: 災事既過，猶追懼未已，故廢宗廟之察，況聞天眚將至，行慶樂之會，於禮乖矣。

translations.literal: After the disaster passed he still pursued fear without end, hence he dropped ancestral inspection—how much more when hearing heaven’s calamity will arrive yet holding a meeting of festive joy—against rite!
translations.idiomatic: Continuing banquets while a sky omen loomed was worse than Lu’s fault.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》所雲諸侯入門不得終禮者，謂日官不豫言，諸侯既入，見蝕乃知耳，非先聞當蝕而朝會不廢也。

translations.literal: What the Record of Rites calls feudal lords entering the gate unable to finish the rite means the day office did not forewarn—after the lords entered they saw the eclipse and knew—not that they heard an eclipse was coming yet did not cancel court.
translations.idiomatic: Cai read the “halted rite” rule as applying to surprise eclipses, not forecast ones.

sentences.zh: 引此，可謂失其義旨。

translations.literal: Citing this, one may say he lost the meaning’s thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Liu misapplied the passage.

sentences.zh: 劉邵所執者《禮記》也，夫子、老聃巷黨之事，亦《禮記》所言，復違而反之，進退無據。

translations.literal: What Liu Shao upheld was the Record of Rites; the Master and Laozi at Lane Party is also spoken in the Record of Rites—yet he violates and reverses it—advance and retreat lack footing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu contradicted the same book he quoted.

sentences.zh: 然荀令所善，漢朝所從，遂使此言至今見稱，莫知其誤矣，後來君子將擬以為式，故正之云爾。

translations.literal: Yet what Director Xun approved, Han followed, has made this statement praised to this day without knowing its error—later gentlemen might take it as model, hence I correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai hoped to stop the bad precedent.

sentences.zh: 」於是冰從眾議，遂以卻會。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Bing followed the majority opinion and postponed the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing canceled court after Cai’s essay.

sentences.zh: 至永和中，殷浩輔政，又欲從劉邵議不卻會。

translations.literal: By Yonghe, Yin Hao as regent again wished to follow Liu Shao’s argument and not postpone assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin Hao wanted Liu’s permissive rule.

sentences.zh: 王彪之據咸寧、建元故事，又曰：「《禮》雲諸侯旅見天子，不得終禮而廢者四，自謂卒暴有之，非為先存其事，而僥倖史官推術繆錯，故不豫廢朝禮也。

translations.literal: Wang Biaozhi cited Xianning and Jianyuan precedent, also saying: “The Rites says when feudal lords travel-audience the Son of Heaven there are four cases where they cannot finish the rite and it is dropped—this refers to sudden crises, not to prior knowledge while hoping astrological technique errs, hence not canceling court in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang argued the four interruptions cover emergencies, not scheduled eclipses.

sentences.zh: 」於是又從彪之議。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they again followed Biaozhi’s opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Court again accepted Wang Biaozhi.

sentences.zh: 《尚書》「禋于六宗」，諸儒互說，往往不同。

translations.literal: The Documents’ “perform yin to the six zong”—various scholars cross-argue, often disagreeing.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists disputed the “six ancestries” for centuries.

sentences.zh: 王莽以《易》六子，遂立六宗祠。

translations.literal: Wang Mang, using the Changes’ six children, then established six-ancestor shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang mapped the cult onto hexagram lines.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝時疑其事，以問王肅，亦以為易六子，故不廢。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi doubted the matter, asked Wang Su, who also held them to be the Changes’ six children—hence they were not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui consulted Wang Su and kept the six shrines.

sentences.zh: 及晉受命，司馬彪等表六宗之祀不應特立新禮，於是遂罷其祀。

translations.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Sima Biao and others memorialized that six-ancestor sacrifice ought not stand apart as new ritual—thereupon its sacrifice was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin briefly abolished the set.

sentences.zh: 其後摯虞奏之，又以為：「案舜受終，'類於上帝，系于六宗，望於山川'，則六宗非上帝之神，又非山川之靈也。

translations.literal: Later Zhi Yu memorialized again, holding: “Examining Shun’s reception of the mandate, ‘sacrificed by category to the Supreme Lord, by line to the six zong, looked toward mountains and rivers’—then the six zong are not the Supreme Lord’s spirits, nor yet mountain-and-river numina.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu cited Shun’s sequence to separate six zong from heaven and peaks.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》肆師職曰：'用牲于社宗。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou’s director of oblations says: ‘use victims at soil zong.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhou pairs “zong” with soil in one clause.

sentences.zh: '黨正職曰：'春秋祭禜亦如之。

translations.literal: The neighborhood head’s duty says: ‘spring and autumn sacrifice zong likewise.’
translations.idiomatic: Local officers also sacrifice to zong seasonally.

sentences.zh: '肆師之宗，與社並列，則班與社同也。

translations.literal: The oblations director’s zong, listed parallel with soil, then ranks the same class as soil.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel wording equates zong with the earth cult’s rank.

sentences.zh: 党正之禜，文不系社，則神與社異也。

translations.literal: The neighborhood head’s zong, text not tied to soil, then the spirit differs from soil.
translations.idiomatic: Village zong rites omit soil, implying a different deity.

sentences.zh: 周之命祀，莫重郊社，宗同於社，則貴神明矣。

translations.literal: Zhou’s commanded sacrifices none rank above suburb and soil; zong matches soil—then it is honored as a bright spirit.
translations.idiomatic: State ritual elevates zong alongside the greatest chthonic cults.

sentences.zh: 又，《月令》孟冬祈于天宗，則《周禮》祭禜，《月令》天宗，六宗之神也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Monthly Ordinance’s first winter prays to heaven’s zong—then the Rites of Zhou’s zong sacrifice, the Monthly Ordinance’s heaven’s zong, are the six zong spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly Ordinance’s “celestial zong” identifies the six.

sentences.zh: 漢光武即位高邑，依《虞書》禋于六宗。

translations.literal: Han Guangwu took the throne at Gaoyi, following the Documents’ yin to six zong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu revived the Shun-era formula at his accession.

sentences.zh: 安帝元初中，立祀乾位，禮同太社。

translations.literal: Andi, early Yuanchu, established sacrifice on the qian position, ritual matching grand soil.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han placed the altar northwest like the great earth mound.

sentences.zh: 魏氏因之，至景初二年，大議其神，朝士紛紜，各有所執。

translations.literal: Wei inherited this; by Jingchu 2 they debated the spirit greatly—court gentlemen wrangled, each clutching a view.
translations.idiomatic: Wei officials fought over definitions in Jingchu 2.

sentences.zh: 惟散騎常侍劉邵以為萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和。

translations.literal: Only cavalier attendant Liu Shao held that the myriad things bear yin and embrace yang, harmonizing breath as harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao offered a metaphysical reading.

sentences.zh: 六宗者，太極沖和之氣，為六氣之宗者也。

translations.literal: The six zong are the Grand Ultimate’s harmonizing breath—what heads the six qi.
translations.idiomatic: He defined them as spirits of cosmic equipoise.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》謂之六宗，《周書》謂之天宗。

translations.literal: The Yu Documents calls them six zong; the Zhou Documents calls them heaven’s zong.
translations.idiomatic: Different books name the same sixfold power.

sentences.zh: 是時考論異同，而從其議。

translations.literal: At that time they examined competing views and followed his thesis.
translations.idiomatic: Wei adopted Liu Shao’s definition.

sentences.zh: 漢魏相仍，著為貴祀。

translations.literal: Han and Wei continued it, recording it as honored sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The cult became a major dynasty-wide observance.

sentences.zh: 凡崇祀百神，放而不至，有其興之，則莫敢廢之。

translations.literal: Generally in exalting sacrifice to the hundred spirits, if loosened yet not carried to excess, once it is raised none dares abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Established rites gain inertia.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，祀六宗如舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix new ritual, sacrificing to six zong as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu asked to restore the full six-shrine round.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ” The edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 《禮》，王為群姓立七祀，曰司命、中霤、國門、國行、大厲、戶、灶。

translations.literal: The Rites: the king for the clans establishes seven sacrifices—called Siming, inner court, state gate, state journey, great plague, door, stove.
translations.idiomatic: Canon lists seven domestic tutelary gods for the royal line.

sentences.zh: 仲春玄鳥至之日，乙太牢祀高禖。

translations.literal: When the dark swallow arrives in mid-spring, sacrifice to High Match with a tai-lao.
translations.idiomatic: Spring’s swallow omen triggered the fertility cult with a great victim.

sentences.zh: 《毛詩》《絲衣篇》，高子曰靈星之屍。

translations.literal: The Mao Odes’ “Silk Robes” piece—Gao says it concerns the spirit impersonator of the Spirit Star.
translations.idiomatic: Mao tradition tied a poem to the agrarian star altar.

sentences.zh: 漢興，高帝亦立靈星祠。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Gaodi also established Spirit Star shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bang copied the star altar.

sentences.zh: 及武帝，以李少君故，始祠灶；

translations.literal: By Wudi, because of Li Shaojun, he first sacrificed to the stove;
translations.idiomatic: Wudi’s kitchen god cult began with a fangshi’s advice.

sentences.zh: 及生戾太子，始立高禖。

translations.literal: when the Heir Apparent Li was born, he first established High Match.
translations.idiomatic: The birth of crown prince Liu Ju brought the matchmaking spirit’s shrine.

sentences.zh: 《漢儀》雲，國家亦有五祀，有司行事，其禮頗輕於社稷，則亦存其典矣。

translations.literal: The Han Observance says the state also has five sacrifices, the offices conducting them; their rite is somewhat lighter than soil-and-grain—thus the canon still survives.
translations.idiomatic: Han statute lists five household cults below the great earth altars in rank yet still on the books.

sentences.zh: 又云，常以仲春之月，立高禖祠于城南，祀以特牲。

translations.literal: It also says, regularly in mid-spring month, establish High Match shrine south of the city, sacrificing with a special victim.
translations.idiomatic: It mandated a spring fertility altar outside the south gate with a singled-out offering.

sentences.zh: 又，是月也，祠老人星于國都南郊老人星廟。

translations.literal: Moreover, that month sacrifice to the elder star at the elder-star shrine south of the capital suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The same month honored Canopus at its southern chapel.

sentences.zh: 立夏祭灶，季秋祠心星于城南壇心星廟。

translations.literal: Summer’s establishment sacrifices to the stove; late autumn sacrifices to the heart star south of the city at the heart-star mound.
translations.idiomatic: They also fed the kitchen god at summer’s start and the “heart” asterism in autumn.

sentences.zh: 元康時，洛陽猶有高禖壇，百姓祠其旁，或謂之落星。

translations.literal: Yuankang era, Luoyang still had a High Match mound; commoners sacrificed beside it, some calling it “falling star.”
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin tourists still called the Luoyang mound a meteor shrine.

sentences.zh: 是後諸祀無聞，江左以來，不立七祀，靈星則配饗南郊，不復特置焉。

translations.literal: Afterward those sacrifices are not heard of; since crossing the river they did not set up the seven sacrifices; Spirit Star was paired in feasting at the southern suburb, no longer separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin folded Spirit Star into the southern sky cult and dropped the seven domestic gods.

sentences.zh: 左氏傳「龍見而雩」，經典尚矣。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary’s “when the dragon appears, perform yu”—the classic affirms it.
translations.idiomatic: Canon backs the spring rain dance when the dragon constellation rises.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，自立春到立夏，盡立秋，郡國尚旱，郡縣各掃除社稷。

translations.literal: Han observance: from spring’s establishment to summer’s establishment through autumn’s establishment, if commanderies and kingdoms still suffer drought, commanderies and counties each sweep soil and grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: Han law ordered local earth shrines swept during prolonged drought.

sentences.zh: 其旱也，公卿官長以次行雩禮求雨，閉諸陽，衣皁，興土龍，立土人，舞僮二佾，七日一變，如故事。

translations.literal: In drought, dukes and ministers and bureau chiefs in turn perform yu rite seeking rain, closing yang outlets, wearing black, raising earthen dragons, setting earthen figures, boy dancers in two rows of eight, changing every seven days, as in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wore black, built clay dragons, and rotated children’s dances weekly.

sentences.zh: 武帝咸寧二年，春久旱。

translations.literal: Wudi, Xianning 2, spring long drought.
translations.idiomatic: A spring drought struck Xianning 2.

sentences.zh: 四月丁已，詔曰「諸旱處廣加祈請」。

translations.literal: Fourth month day dingqi, edict said “where drought is widespread, broadly add prayer and supplication.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered empire-wide rain prayers in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 五月庚午，始祈雨於社稷山川。

translations.literal: Fifth month day gengwu, they first prayed for rain at soil, grain, mountains, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-summer opened joint appeals to earth and landscape gods.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，獲澍雨。

translations.literal: Sixth month day wuzi, soaking rain was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Timely rain fell on wuzi.

sentences.zh: 此雩之舊典也。

translations.literal: This is yu’s old canon.
translations.idiomatic: Such was classical drought ritual.

sentences.zh: 太康三年四月，十年二月，又如之。

translations.literal: Taikang 3 fourth month, Taikang 10 second month, again like this.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 3 and 10 repeated the sequence.

sentences.zh: 其雨多則禜祭，赤幘硃衣，閉諸陰，硃索縈社，伐硃鼓焉。

translations.literal: When rain was excessive they performed yong sacrifice, red kerchiefs and red robes, closed yin outlets, red cords wound the soil altar, beat red drums.
translations.idiomatic: Floods brought red regalia, bound earth gods with crimson rope, and scarlet drums.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》，王者祭昊天上帝、日月星辰、司中司命、風伯雨師、社稷、五土、五嶽、山林川澤、四方百物，兆四類四望，亦如之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: the king sacrifices to August Heaven, sun moon stars, Zhong and Siming, wind elder and rain master, soil and grain, five soils, five marchmounts, mountain forests streams marshes, the four quarters’ hundred things; he sets out four classes and four wang—likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s king catalogued sky, weather, earth, and nature gods in one system.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年六月庚子，初禮五嶽四瀆，咸秩群祀，瘞沈珪璧。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu 2 sixth month day gengzi, first performed rite to five marchmounts and four streams, all ranked group sacrifices, burying and sinking jade disks.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi standardized river and peak cults with submerged jade.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，帝以舟軍入淮。

translations.literal: Sixth year seventh month, the emperor took a fleet into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he sailed the Huai campaign.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，遣使者沈璧于淮。

translations.literal: Ninth month day renxu, he sent envoys to sink a disk in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys drowned a ritual jade in the river that autumn.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和四年八月，帝東巡，遣使者以特牛祠中嶽。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi, Taihe 4 eighth month, the emperor toured east, sending envoys to sacrifice a special ox to the central marchmount.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi’s eastern tour included a Tai Mountain ox.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙元年，行幸長安，使使者以璧幣禮祠華山。

translations.literal: Wei Yuandi, Xixi 1, traveling to Chang’an, sent envoys with disks and silks to perform rite at Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The last Wei emperor honored Mount Hua near Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 及穆帝升平中，何琦論修五嶽祠曰：「唐虞之制，天子五載一巡狩，順時之方，柴燎五嶽，望於山川，遍於群神，故曰，因名山升中於天，所以昭告神祗，饗報功德。

translations.literal: When Mudi, mid-Shengping, He Qi debated repairing five-marchmount shrines: “Tang-Yu’s system had the Son of Heaven tour every five years, following the season’s direction, burning offerings on five marchmounts, gazing toward mountains and rivers, reaching all spirits—hence it is said, by famous mountains announce ascent to heaven—thereby clarifying report to numina and repaying merit.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi quoted sage-king tours that burned on every peak.

sentences.zh: 是以災厲不作，而風雨寒暑以時。

translations.literal: Hence calamity and pestilence did not arise, wind rain cold and heat came on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Orderly seasons followed faithful worship.

sentences.zh: 降及三代，年數雖殊，而其禮不易，五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯，著在經紀，所謂'有其舉之，莫敢廢也。

translations.literal: Down to the three dynasties, though year-counts differed, their rite did not change—five marchmounts ranked with three dukes, four streams with marquises—written in canons—what is called ‘once raised, none dares abolish.’
translations.idiomatic: Later ages kept peaks and rivers tied to noble ranks.

sentences.zh: '及秦漢都西京，涇、渭、長水，雖不在祀典，以近咸陽故，盡得比大川之祠，而正立之祀可以闕哉！

translations.literal: ” When Qin and Han capital was western Chang’an, Jing, Wei, and Chang waters though not in the sacrifice canon, because near Xianyang, all received great-river sacrifice—how can correct established sacrifice be wanting!
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan streams gained great-river status by proximity to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之亂，神州傾覆，茲事替矣。

translations.literal: From Yongjia’s turmoil the heartland overturned; this affair declined.
translations.idiomatic: The southward flight wrecked northern peak cults.

sentences.zh: 惟灊之天柱，在王略之內也，舊台選百戶吏卒，以奉其職。

translations.literal: Only Tianzhu on Mount Qian lay within the royal demesne; old regulations selected a hundred-household garrison to maintain duty.
translations.idiomatic: One Anhui peak still had a token garrison.

sentences.zh: 中興之際，未有官守，廬江郡常遣大吏兼假四時禱賽，春釋寒而冬請冰。

translations.literal: At restoration’s opening there was no official keeper; Lujiang commandery regularly sent a senior clerk doubling seasonal prayer and festival, spring releasing cold, winter requesting ice.
translations.idiomatic: Local magistrates improvised seasonal rites on the mountain.

sentences.zh: 咸和迄今，又復隳替。

translations.literal: From Xianhe until now it again decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Even that lapsed after Xianhe.

sentences.zh: 計今非典之祠，可謂非一。

translations.literal: Counting today’s non-canonical shrines, they are not one only.
translations.idiomatic: Illegal village cults now crowd the map.

sentences.zh: 考其正名，則淫昏之鬼；

translations.literal: Examining their correct names, they are licentious dark ghosts;
translations.idiomatic: Proper names expose them as vulgar spirits.

sentences.zh: 推其糜費，則百姓之蠹。

translations.literal: reckoning their waste, they are parasites on the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Their cost bleeds taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 而山川大神更為簡缺，禮俗穨紊，人神雜擾，公私奔蹙，漸以繁滋。

translations.literal: Yet great spirits of mountains and streams grow more neglected; ritual custom tumbles confused, men and gods mixed and disturbed, public and private squeezed, gradually proliferating.
translations.idiomatic: True landscape gods starve while bogus shrines multiply.

sentences.zh: 良由頃國家多難，日不暇給，草建廢滯，事有未遑。

translations.literal: Truly because lately the state met many hardships, days lacked surplus, makeshift rises and neglects stall—affairs had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: War left no time to regulate worship.

sentences.zh: 今元憝已殲，宜修舊典。

translations.literal: Now the chief villain is slain; it is fitting to repair old canon.
translations.idiomatic: Peace should restore orthodox cults.

sentences.zh: 嶽瀆之域，風教所被，來蘇之眾，咸蒙德澤。

translations.literal: In marchmount and stream regions, where wind and teaching spread, crowds coming to revive all feel virtue’s dew.
translations.idiomatic: River basins await renewed moral sway.

sentences.zh: 而神明禋祀，未之或甄，巡狩柴燎，其廢尚矣。

translations.literal: Yet bright-spirit yin sacrifice is not yet sorted; touring and mountain burning lies long abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Royal tours and peak-burning rites remain in abeyance.

sentences.zh: 崇明前典，將俟皇輿北旋，稽古憲章，大厘制度。

translations.literal: To exalt former canons awaits the imperial carriage’s northward return, examining antiquity and statute, greatly ordering institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Full reform waits on reconquering the north.

sentences.zh: 俎豆牲牢，祝嘏文辭，舊章靡記，可令禮官作式，歸諸誠簡，以達明德馨香，如斯而已。

translations.literal: Stand vessels, victims, invocator blessing phrases—old chapters are lost record—it is fitting to order ritual officers to make models, returning to sincere simplicity, to convey bright virtue’s fragrance—only this.
translations.idiomatic: Officers should draft lean, honest liturgies.

sentences.zh: 其諸襖孽，可粗依法令，先去其甚，俾邪正不黷。

translations.literal: As for various demonic pests, they may roughly follow statutes, first removing the worst, so deviant and correct do not mingle.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaw shrines need pruning by law.

sentences.zh: 」時不見省。

translations.literal: ” At the time it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored He Qi then.

sentences.zh: 昔武王入殷，未及下車而封先代之後，蓋追思其德也。

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu entered Yin, before dismounting the chariot enfeoffed heirs of prior dynasties—thereby pondering their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wu ennobled Shang and Xia lines at once.

sentences.zh: 孔子以大聖而終於陪臣，未有封爵。

translations.literal: Confucius as great sage ended as a minister’s retainer, without enfeoffed rank.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius died without a noble title.

sentences.zh: 至漢元帝，孔霸以帝師賜爵，號褒成君，奉孔子後。

translations.literal: Down to Han Yuandi, Kong Ba because imperial tutor received enfeoffment, titled Lord Bao-cheng, maintaining Confucius’s line.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandi first titled the Kong heir as Lord Bao-cheng.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年正月，詔以議郎孔羨為宗聖侯，邑百戶，奉孔子祀，令魯郡修舊廟，置百戶吏卒以守衛之。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu 2 first month, edict appointed consultant Kong Xian as Marquis of the Ancestral Sage, fief a hundred households, maintaining Confucius sacrifice, ordered Lu commandery to repair the old temple, setting a hundred-household garrison to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi made Kong Xian “Marquis of the Sagely Ancestor” with a temple guard.

sentences.zh: 及武帝泰始三年十一月，改封宗聖侯孔震為奉聖亭侯。

translations.literal: When Wudi, Taishi 3 eleventh month, changed enfeoffment of Marquis of the Ancestral Sage Kong Zhen to Lord of the Altar of the Sagely.
translations.idiomatic: Jin renamed the title to “Lord of the Sagely Altar.”

sentences.zh: 又詔太學及魯國，四時備三牲以祀孔子。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered the Imperial Academy and Lu state each season to prepare three victims for Confucius sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and Qufu both offered three victims seasonally.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧三年，詔給奉聖亭侯孔亭四時祠孔子祭直，如泰始故事。

translations.literal: Mingdi, Taining 3, edict granted Lord of the Sagely Altar Kong Ting the seasonal Confucius sacrifice allowance, as in Taishi precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi funded Kong Ting’s offerings like Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 故事，祀皋陶于廷尉寺，新禮移祀於律署，以同祭先聖於太學也。

translations.literal: By precedent they sacrificed to Gao Yao at the commandant of justice office; the new ritual moved sacrifice to the law bureau, to match sacrificing to the former sage at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Reform moved the judge-god beside the law office to mirror Confucius at the academy.

sentences.zh: 故事，祀以社日，新禮改以孟秋之月，以應秋政。

translations.literal: By precedent sacrifice used soil day; the new ritual changed to first autumn month, to match autumn’s punitive government.
translations.idiomatic: Date shifted from earth festival to early autumn.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「案《虞書》，皋陶作士師，惟明克允，國重其功，人思其當，是以獄官禮其神，系者致其祭，功在斷獄之成，不在律令之始也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: “Examining the Yu Documents, Gao Yao served as minister of punishments, enlightened and trustworthy, the state weighted his merit, people pondered his fitness—hence prison officials ritualize his spirit, the bound offer him sacrifice—merit lay in completing judgments, not in the start of codified law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued Gao Yao’s cult honored verdicts, not statute drafting.

sentences.zh: 大學之設，義重太常，故祭於太學，是崇聖而從重也。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy’s establishment, meaning weighty as grand master of ceremonies—hence sacrifice at the Imperial Academy—this exalts the sage and follows what is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The academy ranks with high ritual, deserving the sage’s altar.

sentences.zh: 律署之置，卑于廷尉，移祀於署，是去重而就輕也。

translations.literal: The law bureau’s placement is lower than the commandant of justice; moving sacrifice to the bureau is leaving weight for lightness.
translations.idiomatic: The law office sat below the high court; moving the cult there demoted the god.

sentences.zh: 律非正署，廢興無常，宜如舊祀于廷尉。

translations.literal: Law is not a main bureau, abolition and rise lacks constancy—it is fitting to sacrifice as before at the commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu wanted Gao Yao back at the justice ministry.

sentences.zh: 又，祭用仲春，義取重生，改用孟秋，以應刑殺，理未足以相易。

translations.literal: Moreover sacrifice used mid-spring, meaning taking rebirth; changing to first autumn to match execution and killing—principle insufficient to exchange them.
translations.idiomatic: Spring honored life; autumn matched executions—ill fit for a trial god.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，皆如舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix new ritual entirely like the old.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to revert both site and season.

translations.literal: ” Ruling: “Approved.”
translations.idiomatic: The edict said yes.

sentences.zh: 歲旦常設葦茭桃梗，磔雞于宮及百寺之門，以禳惡氣。

translations.literal: New Year’s dawn regularly set reed bundles and peach switches, split cocks at palace and hundred offices’ gates, to expel malign qi.
translations.idiomatic: Year’s first morning planted peach charms and killed roosters at every gate.

sentences.zh: 案漢儀則仲夏設之，有桃印，無磔雞。

translations.literal: Examining Han observance, mid-summer set them, with peach seals, no split cocks.
translations.idiomatic: Han used midsummer peach plaques without cock sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 及魏明帝大修禳禮，故何晏禳祭議雞特牲供禳釁之事。

translations.literal: When Wei Mingdi greatly expanded expulsion rites, hence He Yan’s expulsion-sacrifice discussion used cocks as special victims for expulsion and smearing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei added roosters under He Yan’s rules.

sentences.zh: 磔雞宜起于魏，桃印本漢制，所以輔卯金，又宜魏所除也。

translations.literal: Split cock likely began with Wei; peach seal stems from Han system, meant to bolster the Mao-metal house—again something Wei ought to have removed.
translations.idiomatic: Peach amulets supported Han’s “Liu” prophecy; Wei kept some Han exorcism toys.

sentences.zh: 但未詳改仲夏在歲旦之所起耳。

translations.literal: Yet it is not clear when mid-summer shifted to New Year’s dawn.
translations.idiomatic: No one recorded why the date moved to New Year.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍元年，詔郡國，山川不在祀典者勿祠。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi, Qinglong 1, edict to commanderies and kingdoms: mountains and rivers not in the sacrifice canon—do not sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui banned unlisted landscape cults.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始元年十二月，詔曰：「昔聖帝明王修五嶽四瀆，名山川澤，各有定制，所以報陰陽之功故也。

translations.literal: Wudi, Taishi 1 twelfth month, edict said: “Formerly sage emperors and enlightened kings cultivated five marchmounts and four streams, famous mountains, streams, and marshes, each having fixed regulation—thereby repaying yin and yang’s work.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan opened his reign by listing orthodox nature gods.

sentences.zh: 然以道蒞天下者，其鬼不神，其神不傷人，故祝史薦而無愧辭，是以其人敬慎幽冥而淫祀不作。

translations.literal: Yet one who faces the realm with the Way—their ghosts are not uncanny, their spirits do not harm people—hence invocators present offerings without shameful phrases—therefore people revere and heed the hidden world and licentious sacrifice does not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous rule keeps spirits mild and folk religion sober.

sentences.zh: 末世通道不篤，僭禮瀆神，縱欲祈請，曾不敬而遠之，徒偷以求幸，襖妄相煽，舍正為邪，故魏朝疾之。

translations.literal: In degenerate ages the Way is not deep, usurping rite affronts spirits, wantonly praying and begging, never reverently keeping distance, vainly stealing to seek luck, omens and delusions fan one another, abandoning straight for crooked—hence Wei court detested it.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han licentious shrines drew Wei’s purge.

sentences.zh: 其案舊禮具為之制，使功著於人者必有其報，而襖淫之鬼不亂其間。

translations.literal: Let old ritual be examined and fully regulated, so those whose merit shines on people must have repayment, while demonic licentious ghosts do not intrude among them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin would reward true benefactor gods and ban impostors.

sentences.zh: 」二年正月，有司奏春分祠厲殃及禳祠，詔曰：「不在祀典，除之。」

translations.literal: ” Second year first month, offices memorialized spring equinox cult to plague-harm and expulsion sacrifice; edict said “not in sacrifice canon—remove them.”
translations.idiomatic: A later edict struck unlisted plague rites.

sentences.zh: 《王制》，天子七廟，諸侯以下各有等差，禮文詳矣。

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations: Son of Heaven seven temples, marquises downward each have graded difference—ritual text is detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations cap royal shrines at seven.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝建安十八年五月，以河北十郡封魏武帝為魏公。

translations.literal: Han Xiandi, Jian’an 18 fifth month, enfeoffed Wei Martial Emperor with ten commanderies north of the Yellow River as duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xian made Cao Cao duke of ten Hebei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，始建宗廟於鄴，自以諸侯禮立五廟也。

translations.literal: That year seventh month, first built ancestral temple at Ye, on his own taking feudal rite establishing five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao raised five lineage halls as a feudatory.

sentences.zh: 後雖進爵為王，無所改易。

translations.literal: Later although advanced in rank to king, nothing was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Kingship kept the five-shrine layout.

sentences.zh: 延康元年，文帝繼王位，七月，追尊皇祖為大王，丁夫人曰大王后。

translations.literal: Yankang 1, Wendi succeeded king seventh month, posthumously honored imperial grandfather as great king, Lady Ding as great queen.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi elevated grandfather and Lady Ding when he took the Wei throne-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 黃初元年十一月受禪，又追尊大王曰大皇帝，皇考武王曰武皇帝。

translations.literal: Huangchu 1 eleventh month receiving abdication, again posthumously honored great king as grand emperor, imperial father Martial King as Martial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Han’s cession he raised Cao Song and Cao Cao’s temple names.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，以洛京宗廟未成，乃祠武帝於建始殿，親執饋奠，如家人禮。

translations.literal: Second year sixth month, because Luoyang ancestral temple was not yet finished, they sacrificed to Martial Emperor at the Jianshi Hall, personally bearing offerings like family rite.
translations.idiomatic: He fed Cao Cao in a palace hall like a private wake.

sentences.zh: 案《禮》將營宮室，宗廟為先，庶人無廟，故祭於寢，帝者行之非禮甚矣。

translations.literal: Examining the Rites: when about to build palaces, ancestral temple comes first; commoners lack temples, hence sacrifice in the chamber—an emperor practicing this is greatly against rite.
translations.idiomatic: The digest criticizes palace-room sacrifice as fit only for commoners.

sentences.zh: 明帝太和三年六月，又追尊高祖大長秋曰高皇，夫人吳氏曰高皇后，並在鄴廟。

translations.literal: Mingdi, Taihe 3 sixth month, again posthumously honored great-grandfather grand chamberlain as Gao Emperor, Lady Wu as Gao Empress, both in Ye temple.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui added remote ancestors to the Ye complex.

sentences.zh: 廟所祠，則文帝之高祖處士、曾祖高皇、祖大皇帝共一廟，考太祖武皇帝特一廟，百世不毀，然則所祠止於親廟四室也。

translations.literal: What the temple worshiped: Wendi’s great-great-grandfather recluse, great-grandfather Gao Emperor, grandfather Grand Emperor shared one temple; father dynastic founder Martial Emperor had a separate temple, not destroyed for a hundred generations—thus what was worshiped stopped at four intimate-temple chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Four bays held recent lines; Martial Emperor stood alone forever.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，洛京廟成，則以親盡遷處士主置園邑，使行太傅太常韓暨、行太常宗正曹恪持節迎高皇以下神主，共一廟，猶為四室而已。

translations.literal: That year eleventh month, when Luoyang temple was completed, because affection ended they moved the recluse’s tablet to a garden estate, ordered acting grand tutor grand master of ceremonies Han Ji and acting grand master of ceremonies director of imperial clan Cao Ke, bearing insignia, to welcome Gao Emperor downward spirit tablets, sharing one temple—still only four chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang completion shifted distant tablets to a park shrine but kept four indoor bays.

sentences.zh: 至景初元年六月，群公有司始更奏定七廟之制，曰：「大魏三聖相承，以成帝業。

translations.literal: By Jingchu 1 sixth month, dukes and offices first re-memorialized fixing seven-temple system, saying: “Great Wei’s three sages succeeded one another, completing imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu reform proclaimed three eternal Wei ancestors.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝肇建洪基，撥亂夷險，為魏太祖。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor founded the great foundation, quelled chaos and smoothed peril, serving as Wei dynastic founder.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao became “Founding Ancestor.”

sentences.zh: 文皇帝繼天革命，應期受禪，為魏高祖。

translations.literal: Civil Emperor inherited heaven’s reordering, met the period and received abdication, serving as Wei Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi became “High Ancestor.”

sentences.zh: 上集成大命，清定華夏，興制禮樂，宜為魏烈祖。

translations.literal: The present sovereign completes the great mandate, pacifies Huaxia, raises institutions of ritual and music—fitting to be Wei Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui took the title “Fiery Ancestor.”

sentences.zh: 于太祖廟北為二祧，其左為文帝廟，號曰高祖昭祧，其右擬明帝，號曰烈祖穆祧。

translations.literal: North of the Founding Ancestor temple build two distant shrines: left Wendi temple, titled Gaozu Bright Distant Shrine; right planning for Mingdi, titled Liezu Sombre Distant Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking halls housed Cao Pi and reserved Cao Rui’s line.

sentences.zh: 三祖之廟，萬世不毀。

translations.literal: The three ancestors’ temples are never destroyed for myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: Three shrines gained perpetual worship.

sentences.zh: 其餘四廟，親盡迭遷，一如周後稷、文武廟祧之禮。」

translations.literal: The remaining four temples, when affection ends, rotate removal—just like Zhou’s Hou Ji, Wen, and Wu temple distant-shrine rite.”
translations.idiomatic: Four lesser bays would cycle like Zhou’s removal system.

sentences.zh: 文帝甄後賜死，故不列廟。

translations.literal: Wendi’s Empress Zhen was ordered to die—hence she was not listed in temple.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhen’s disgrace kept her off the main altar.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，有司奏請追諡曰文昭皇后，使司空王朗持節奉策告祠於陵。

translations.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, offices memorialized requesting posthumous title as Civil and Radiant Empress, ordering Minister of Works Wang Lang bearing insignia to present the patent and announce cult at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui rehabilitated his mother’s name at her mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三公又奏曰：「自古周人歸祖後稷，又特立廟以祀薑嫄。

translations.literal: The three excellencies again memorialized: “From antiquity Zhou people traced ancestor to Hou Ji, also separately built temple to sacrifice to Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers compared her to Jiang Yuan’s side shrine.

sentences.zh: 今文昭皇后之于後嗣，聖德至化，豈有量哉！

translations.literal: Now Civil and Radiant Empress’s relation to posterity—sagely virtue and transforming influence—how can it be measured!
translations.idiomatic: They praised her moral legacy to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夫以皇家世妃之尊，神靈遷化，而無寢廟以承享祀，非以報顯德，昭孝敬也。

translations.literal: Given an imperial consort line’s honor, spirit transformed, yet no bed-chamber temple to receive feasting sacrifice—this is not how to repay manifest virtue or clarify filial respect.
translations.idiomatic: She lacked an indoor shrine despite her rank.

sentences.zh: 稽之古制，宜依周禮，別立寢廟。

translations.literal: Examining ancient system, it is fitting to follow Zhou rite and separately establish bed-chamber temple.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for a separate mortuary shrine in Zhou style.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: ” Memorial approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 太和元年二月，立廟於鄴。

translations.literal: Taihe 1 second month, established temple at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ye gained her chapel in Taihe 1.

sentences.zh: 四月，洛邑初營宗廟，掘地得玉璽，方一寸九分，其文曰「天子羨思慈親。

translations.literal: Fourth month, when Luoyang first built ancestral temple, digging earth they obtained a jade seal one cun nine fen square, its inscription reading “The Son of Heaven yearns for his kind mother.
translations.idiomatic: Builders unearthed a seal blessing maternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 」明帝為之改容，乙太牢告廟。

translations.literal: ” Mingdi changed expression, sacrificed with tai-lao to announce at temple.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, he offered a great victim in report.

sentences.zh: 至景初元年十二月己未，有司又奏文昭皇后立廟京師，永傳享祀，樂舞與祖廟同，廢鄴廟。

translations.literal: By Jingchu 1 twelfth month day jiwei, offices again memorialized Civil and Radiant Empress establishing temple in the capital, eternally transmitting feasting sacrifice, music and dance matching dynastic temples, abolishing Ye temple.
translations.idiomatic: Her cult moved to Luoyang with full music; Ye closed.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙元年，進文帝爵為王，追命舞陽宣文侯為宣王，忠武侯為景王。

translations.literal: Wei Yuandi, Xixi 1, advanced Wendi’s rank to king, posthumously naming Wuyang Lord Xuanwen as King Xuan, loyal martial lord as King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The final Wei ruler elevated Sima Zhao and his forebears.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，文帝崩，諡曰文王。

translations.literal: That year eighth month, Wendi died, posthumous title King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao died that autumn as “King Wen.”

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始元年十二月丙寅，受禪，丁卯，追尊皇祖宣王為宣皇帝，伯考景王為景皇帝，考文王為文皇帝，宣王妃張氏為宣穆皇后，景王夫人羊氏為景皇后。

translations.literal: Wudi, Taishi 1 twelfth month day bingyin, received abdication; dingmao, posthumously honored imperial grandfather King Xuan as Emperor Xuan, paternal uncle King Jing as Emperor Jing, father King Wen as Emperor Wen, King Xuan’s consort Lady Zhang as Empress Xuanmu, King Jing’s consort Lady Yang as Empress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan’s first act raised three generations of Sima kings to emperors and titled their wives.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，有司奏置七廟。

translations.literal: Second year first month, the offices memorialized to set seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers asked for the full seven-shrine Zhou layout.

sentences.zh: 帝重其役，詔宜權立一廟。

translations.literal: The emperor thought the labor heavy; edict said it was fitting provisionally to erect one temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi shrank the project to one building for economy.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣議奏：「上古清廟一宮，尊遠神祗。

translations.literal: Thereupon ministers debated and memorialized: “In high antiquity the pure temple was one palace, honoring distant numina.
translations.idiomatic: They cited the single-hall model of high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 逮至周室，制為七廟，以辯宗祧。

translations.literal: Down to Zhou’s house, they made seven temples to distinguish main line from distant shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had multiplied halls for genealogical clarity.

sentences.zh: 聖旨深弘，遠跡上世，敦崇唐虞，舍七廟之繁華，遵一宮之遠旨。

translations.literal: The sagely decree is profoundly broad, tracing footprints to high antiquity, honoring Tang and Yu, discarding seven temples’ extravagance, following one palace’s distant intent.
translations.idiomatic: They flattered his choice to imitate Shun’s frugality.

sentences.zh: 昔舜承堯禪，受終文祖，遂陟帝位，蓋三十載，月正元日，又格于文祖，遂陟帝位，此則虞氏不改唐廟，因仍舊宮。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun received Yao’s abdication, received completion at Wen’s ancestor, then ascended the throne—some thirty years—first month proper day first of year, again arrived at Wen’s ancestor, then ascended the throne—this shows the Yu house did not alter Tang’s temple but continued the old palace.
translations.idiomatic: They argued Shun kept Yao’s hall, so Jin could keep Wei’s.

sentences.zh: 可依有虞氏故事，即用魏廟。

translations.literal: It may follow Youyu’s precedent, immediately using Wei’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: Reuse Cao Wei’s ancestral complex.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: ” Memorial approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 於是追祭征西將軍、豫章府君、潁川府君、京兆府君，與宣皇帝、景皇帝、文皇帝為三昭三穆。

translations.literal: Thereupon they posthumously sacrificed to General Who Conquers the West, Lord of Yuzhang, Lord of Yingchuan, Lord of Jingzhao, together with Emperors Xuan, Jing, and Wen as three bright and three somber positions.
translations.idiomatic: Six forebears plus three emperors filled the six alternating niches.

sentences.zh: 是時宣皇未升，太祖虛位，所以祠六世，與景帝為七廟，其禮則據王肅說也。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan had not yet ascended; dynastic founder’s seat stood empty—therefore they worshiped six generations, and with Emperor Jing made seven temples—the rite followed Wang Su’s explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su’s count left the founder’s bay open until Xuan’s tablet rose.

sentences.zh: 七月，又詔曰：「主者前奏，就魏舊廟，誠亦有准。

translations.literal: Seventh month, another edict said: “The responsible office earlier memorialized taking Wei’s old temple—indeed there is precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi had second thoughts about reusing Wei brickwork.

sentences.zh: 然於祗奉神明，情猶未安，宜更營造。

translations.literal: Yet in respectfully serving numinous spirits, feeling is still unsettled—it is fitting to build anew.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a fresh Jin temple.

sentences.zh: 」於是改創宗廟。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they rebuilt the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Construction began on Jin’s own hall.

sentences.zh: 十一月，追尊景帝夫人夏侯氏為景懷皇后。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, posthumously honored Emperor Jing’s consort Lady Xiahou as Empress Jinghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi’s wife gained empress honors.

sentences.zh: 任茂議以為夏侯初嬪之時，未有王業。

translations.literal: Ren Mao argued that when Lady Xiahou first became consort, royal enterprise had not yet existed.
translations.idiomatic: A critic said she predated the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi overruled the objection.

sentences.zh: 太康元年，靈壽公主修麗祔于太廟，周漢未有其准。

translations.literal: Taikang 1, Princess Lingshou Xiuli was joined in the grand temple—Zhou and Han lacked this standard.
translations.idiomatic: A princess received main-hall placement without classical warrant.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝則別立平原主廟，晉又異魏也。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi separately built Princess Pingyuan’s temple; Jin again differed from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ming of Wei had given his daughter a side shrine; Jin folded her in.

sentences.zh: 六年，因廟陷，當改修創，群臣又議奏曰：「古者七廟異所，自宜如禮。

translations.literal: Sixth year, because the temple collapsed, when rebuilding and founding, ministers again debated and memorialized: “Anciently seven temples had separate sites—it is fitting to follow rite.
translations.idiomatic: Collapse triggered debate on seven separate buildings.

sentences.zh: 」詔又曰：「古雖七廟，自近代以來皆一廟七室，於禮無廢，於情為敘，亦隨時之宜也。

translations.literal: ” Edict again said: “Anciently though seven temples, from recent generations onward all are one temple with seven chambers—nothing in rite forbids it, in sentiment it is orderly—also following the times’ suitability.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi preferred one building with seven bays.

sentences.zh: 其便仍舊。

translations.literal: Let it remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the single-complex plan.

sentences.zh: 」至十年，乃更改築于宣陽門內，窮極壯麗，然坎位之制猶如初爾。

translations.literal: ” By the tenth year they changed construction inside Xuanyang Gate, extremely grand and splendid, yet the north-quarter layout remained as at first.
translations.idiomatic: A lavish rebuild still faced the canonical direction.

sentences.zh: 廟成，帝用摯虞議，率百官遷神主於新廟，自征西以下，車服導從皆如帝者之儀。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, the emperor adopted Zhi Yu’s proposal, leading hundred officials to move spirit tablets to the new temple; from General Who Conquers the West downward, chariot dress and escort all followed imperial ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Tablet procession mimicked an imperial cortege.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩則遷征西，及惠帝崩又遷豫章。

translations.literal: When Wudi died then they moved General Who Conquers the West; when Huidi died again they moved Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Deaths triggered removal of oldest tablets per rule.

sentences.zh: 而惠帝世湣懷太子、太子二子哀太孫臧、沖太孫尚並祔廟，元帝世，懷帝殤太子又祔廟，號為陰室四殤。

translations.literal: In Huidi’s reign Prince Minhuai, the heir’s two sons—mourning eldest grandson Zang and youngest grandson Shang—were all joined in temple; in Yuandi’s reign, Emperor Huai’s dead crown prince was also joined—called the four dead infants of the yin chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Child heirs received shadow niches outside normal rotation.

sentences.zh: 懷帝初，又策諡武帝楊後曰武悼皇后，改葬峻陽陵側，別祠弘訓宮，不列於廟。

translations.literal: Early in Huai’s reign they again decreed posthumous title for Wudi’s Empress Yang as Martial and Mournful Empress, reburied beside Junyang tumulus, separately culted at Hongxun Palace, not listed in the main temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi’s rehabilitated cult stayed apart from the seven bays.

sentences.zh: 元帝既即尊位，上繼武帝，於元為禰，如漢光武上繼元帝故事也。

translations.literal: When Yuandi took supreme rank, continuing Wudi, in generational terms he was “father”—like Han Guangwu continuing Emperor Yuan’s story.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui claimed spiritual succession to Sima Yan like Guangwu to Western Han.

sentences.zh: 是時，西京神主，堙滅虜庭，江左建廟，皆更新造。

translations.literal: At that time western capital spirit tablets were buried or lost in barbarian courts; building temples south of the river, all were newly made.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin carved fresh tablets for everyone.

sentences.zh: 尋以登懷帝之主，又遷潁川，位雖七室，其實五世，蓋從刁協以兄弟為世數故也。

translations.literal: Soon after installing Emperor Huai’s tablet, again they moved Yingchuan—though positions numbered seven chambers, in fact five generations—because they followed Diao Xie’s counting brothers as generations.
translations.idiomatic: Diao’s brother-count rule emptied two niches prematurely.

sentences.zh: 于時百度草創，舊禮未備，毀主權居別室。

translations.literal: At that time every regulation was founding draft, old rite not complete—destroyed tablets were temporarily housed in a side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Removed tablets sat in limbo.

sentences.zh: 至太興三年正月乙卯，詔曰：「吾雖上繼世祖，然於懷、湣皇帝皆北面稱臣。

translations.literal: By Taixing 3 first month day yimao, edict said: “Although I continue Shizu, toward Emperors Huai and Min I faced north as subject.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandi admitted he had been vassal to the last two Luoyang emperors.

sentences.zh: 今祠太廟，不親執觴酌，而令有司行事，於情禮不安。

translations.literal: Now sacrificing at the grand temple, not personally bearing cup and ladle but ordering the office to conduct the affair—in feeling and rite this is unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: He felt wrong delegating pour at his former lords’ tablets.

sentences.zh: 可依禮更處。
