translations.idiomatic: He sought a ritual fix.

sentences.zh: 」太常恆議：「今聖上繼武皇帝，宜准漢世祖故事，不親執觴爵。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Heng proposed: “Now the sage above continues Martial Emperor—it is fitting to follow Han Guangwu’s story, not personally bearing sacrificial cups.
translations.idiomatic: One faction cited Guangwu’s hands-off model.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「今上承繼武帝，而廟之昭穆，四世而已，前太常賀循、博士傅純，並以為惠、懷及湣，宜別立廟。

translations.literal: ” Another said: “Now the sovereign continues Wudi, yet the temple’s bright and somber count only four generations; former chamberlain He Xun and erudite Fu Chun both held that Hui, Huai, and Min ought separately to receive temples.
translations.idiomatic: Others wanted three exiled emperors split off.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚謂廟室當以容主為限，無拘常數。

translations.literal: Yet your servant foolishly holds temple chambers ought to be limited by capacity to hold tablets, not bound to a constant number.
translations.idiomatic: Heng argued room count should flex with tablets.

sentences.zh: 殷世有二祖三宗，若拘七室，則當祭禰而已。

translations.literal: Yin age had two founders and three honored kings—if bound to seven chambers, one would sacrifice only to father.
translations.idiomatic: Shang precedent showed more than seven worthies.

sentences.zh: 推此論之，宜還復豫章、潁川，全祠七廟之禮。

translations.literal: Pushing this reasoning, it is fitting to restore Yuzhang and Yingchuan, fully performing seven-temple rite.
translations.idiomatic: Restore removed forebears to fill seven lines.

sentences.zh: 」驃騎長史溫嶠議：「凡言兄弟不相入廟，既非禮文，且光武奮劍振起，不策名于孝平，務神其事，以應九世之讖，又古不共廟，故別立焉。

translations.literal: ” General of Agile Cavalry chief clerk Wen Jiao proposed: “Whenever it says brothers do not enter one temple—that is not ritual text; moreover Guangwu raised sword and rose, not enrolling his name under Emperor Ping, striving to spiritize the affair to match the nine-generation prophecy; moreover antiquity did not share temples—hence he separately built.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao distinguished Sima Rui from Guangwu’s usurpation narrative.

sentences.zh: 今上以策名而言，殊于光武之事，躬奉蒸嘗，於經既正，于情又安矣。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign, speaking by enrolled name, differs from Guangwu’s affair; personally presenting steam offerings is correct in canon and settled in sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandi had legitimate title to pour wine himself.

sentences.zh: 太常恆欲還二府君，以全七世，嶠謂是宜。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Heng wished to restore the two lords to complete seven generations; Jiao said this was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Both agreed to reinstate two tablets.

sentences.zh: 」驃騎將軍王導從嶠議。

translations.literal: ” General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao followed Jiao’s proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao backed Wen Jiao.

sentences.zh: 嶠又曰：「其非子者，可直言皇帝敢告某皇帝，又若以一帝為一世，則不祭禰，反不及庶人。

translations.literal: Jiao also said: “For those not in direct son-line, one may straightly say ‘Emperor dares announce to such-and-such Emperor’; if one emperor counts as one generation, then one does not sacrifice to father—falling short even of commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He warned against skipping the father line.

sentences.zh: 」帝從嶠議，悉施用之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed Jiao’s proposals, employing them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui adopted the full program.

sentences.zh: 於是乃更定制，還復豫章、潁川于昭穆之位，以同惠帝嗣武故事，而惠、懷、湣三帝自從《春秋》尊尊之義，在廟不替也。

translations.literal: Thereupon they revised regulation, restoring Yuzhang and Yingchuan to bright and somber positions, matching Huidi’s succession to Wu’s story, while Hui, Huai, and Min three emperors on their own follow Spring and Autumn’s exaltation of rank—remaining in temple without replacement.
translations.idiomatic: The three tragic emperors kept permanent side niches.

sentences.zh: 及元帝崩，則豫章復遷。

translations.literal: When Yuandi died, then Yuzhang was moved again.
translations.idiomatic: Another death cycle bumped Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 然元帝神位猶在湣帝之下，故有坎室者十也。

translations.literal: Yet Yuandi’s spirit seat still stood below Emperor Min—hence there were ten niche positions.
translations.idiomatic: Genealogy chaos filled ten bays.

sentences.zh: 至明帝崩，而穎川又遷，猶十室也。

translations.literal: When Mingdi died, then Yingchuan again moved—still ten chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi’s death still left ten slots in use.

sentences.zh: 于時續廣太廟，故三遷主並還西儲，名之曰祧，以准遠廟。

translations.literal: At that time they extended the grand temple, so three moved tablets together returned to western storage, called distant shrine, matching far-temple precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Expanded west wing held “distant” tablets.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康七年五月，始作武悼皇后神主，祔於廟，配饗世祖。

translations.literal: Chengdi, Xianning 7 fifth month, first fashioned Martial and Mournful Empress’s spirit tablet, joined in temple, paired in feasting with Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi entered the hall under Chengdi.

sentences.zh: 成帝崩而康帝承統，以兄弟一世，故不遷京兆，始十一室也。

translations.literal: When Chengdi died and Kangdi continued the line, as brothers sharing one generation, they did not move Jingzhao—beginning eleven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Brother emperors froze one removal step, swelling to eleven.

sentences.zh: 至康帝崩，穆帝立，永和二年七月，有司奏：「十月殷祭，京兆府君當遷祧室。

translations.literal: When Kangdi died and Mudi succeeded, Yonghe 2 seventh month, offices memorialized: “Tenth month’s yin offering, Jingzhao lord ought to move to distant chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe 2 scheduled Jingzhao’s retirement.

sentences.zh: 昔征西、豫章、潁川三府君毀主，中興之初權居天府，在廟門之西。

translations.literal: Formerly General Who Conquers the West, Yuzhang, and Yingchuan three lords’ destroyed tablets, at restoration’s opening were temporarily housed in the celestial treasury west of temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Old removed tablets had lived in a western closet.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，太常馮懷錶續奉還于西儲夾室，謂之為祧，疑亦非禮。

translations.literal: In Xianning, Grand Master of Ceremonies Feng Huai memorialized continuing to return them to western storage flanking chambers, calling it distant shrine—doubtful whether this matches rite.
translations.idiomatic: Feng’s relabeling them a distant shrine was questioned.

sentences.zh: 今京兆遷入，是為四世遠祖，長在太祖之上。

translations.literal: Now Jingzhao enters—this makes four generations of distant ancestors, permanently above the dynastic founder.
translations.idiomatic: The math put remote lords above Sima Yi’s seat.

sentences.zh: 昔周室太祖世遠，故遷有所歸。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou’s house’s dynastic founder generations were distant—hence removal had somewhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s deep pedigree justified stacking.

sentences.zh: 今晉廟宣皇為主。

translations.literal: Now Jin temple takes Emperor Xuan as root.
translations.idiomatic: Jin anchored on Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 而四祖居之，是屈祖就孫也；

translations.literal: Yet four ancestors occupy it—this bends ancestors to grandsons;
translations.idiomatic: Four lines sat above their descendant’s founder title.

sentences.zh: 殷祫在上，是代太祖也。

translations.literal: yin offering in the upper hall replaces the dynastic founder.
translations.idiomatic: The great colligation rite would demote the founder’s role.

sentences.zh: 」領司徒蔡謨議：「四府君宜改築別室，若未展者，當入就太廟之室，人莫敢卑其祖，文武不先不窋。

translations.literal: ” Overseeing Minister of Education Cai Mo proposed: “The four lords ought to have separate chambers built; if not yet expanded, they should enter the grand temple’s chambers—no one dares demean his ancestor; King Wen and King Wu do not rank before Buzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo cited Zhou kings honoring distant line.

sentences.zh: 殷祭之日，征西東面，處宣皇之上。

translations.literal: On yin offering day, General Who Conquers the West faces east, placed above Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: West-general tablet would sit north of Xuan in the big service.

sentences.zh: 其後遷廟之主，藏於征西之祧，祭薦不絕。

translations.literal: Later moved tablets are stored in General Who Conquers the West’s distant shrine—offerings continue without break.
translations.idiomatic: Removed tablets stayed in the western distant shrine with seasonal grain.

sentences.zh: 」護軍將軍馮懷議：「禮，無廟者為壇以祭，可立別室藏之，至殷禘則祭於壇也。

translations.literal: ” Guards general Feng Huai proposed: “Rite: where there is no temple, make an earthen altar to sacrifice—may build separate chamber to store them; at yin and di they sacrifice at the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Feng suggested altar storage for distant tablets.

sentences.zh: 」輔國將軍譙王司馬無忌等議：「諸儒謂太王、王季遷主，藏于文武之祧。

translations.literal: ” Support-the-Army General Prince of Qiao Sima Wuji and others proposed: “Various scholars say King Tai and King Ji’s moved tablets were hidden in Wen and Wu’s distant shrine.
translations.idiomatic: They quoted Zhou storage of early kings.

sentences.zh: 如此，府君遷主宜在宣帝廟中。

translations.literal: In this way the lord’s moved tablet ought to be inside Emperor Xuan’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: Jin tablets should nest under Xuan.

sentences.zh: 然今無寢室，宜變通而改築。

translations.literal: Yet now there is no bed chamber—it is fitting to adapt flexibly and rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: More architecture was needed.

sentences.zh: 又殷祫太廟，征西東面。

translations.literal: Moreover at yin offering in grand temple, General Who Conquers the West faces east.
translations.idiomatic: East-facing seat repeated for the grand rite.

sentences.zh: 」尚書郎孫綽與無忌議同，曰：「太祖雖位始九五，而道以從暢，替人爵之尊，篤天倫之道，所以成教本而光百代也。

translations.literal: ” Masters of Writing aide Sun Chuo agreed with Wuji, saying: “Although dynastic founder’s position began at the ninth five, his way followed smooth expansion, setting aside human rank’s honor, deepening heaven-human ties—thereby completing instruction’s root and shining for hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Sun defended Sima Yi’s moral precedence over seat order.

sentences.zh: 」尚書郎徐禪議：「《禮》'去祧為壇，去壇為墠'，歲祫則祭之。

translations.literal: ” Masters of Writing aide Xu Chan proposed: “The Rites says ‘leaving distant shrine makes altar, leaving altar makes cleared field’—yearly offering then sacrifices them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu cited the altar-and-field downgrade chain.

sentences.zh: 今四祖遷主，可藏之石室，有禱則祭於壇墠。

translations.literal: Now four ancestors’ moved tablets may be hidden in a stone chamber; when there is prayer then sacrifice at altar or field.
translations.idiomatic: Stone crypt plus occasional altar rites.

sentences.zh: 」又遣禪至會稽，訪處士虞喜。

translations.literal: ” They also sent Chan to Kuaiji to consult recluse Yu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chan consulted Yu Xi.

sentences.zh: 喜答曰：「漢世韋玄成等以毀主瘞于園，魏朝議者雲應埋兩階之間。

translations.literal: Xi replied: “Han-era Wei Xuancheng and others buried destroyed tablets in the park; Wei court debaters said they should be buried between two steps.
translations.idiomatic: Yu listed Han-Wei burial spots for old tablets.

sentences.zh: 且神主本在太廟，若今別室而祭，則不如永藏。

translations.literal: Moreover spirit tablets originally lay in grand temple; if now separately chambered and sacrificed, it is not as good as permanent hiding.
translations.idiomatic: He preferred sealing them away.

sentences.zh: 又四君無追號之禮，益明應毀而無祭。

translations.literal: Moreover the four lords lack posthumous-elevation rite—this clarifies they should be destroyed without sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They never received full emperor honors.

sentences.zh: 」是時簡文為撫軍、與尚書郎劉邵等奏：「四祖同居西祧，藏主石室，禘祫及祭，如先朝舊儀。

translations.literal: ” At that time Prince of Kuaiji as regional commander, with Masters of Writing aide Liu Shao and others memorialized: “Four ancestors together dwell in western distant shrine, storing tablets in stone chamber; di and yin offerings follow former court’s old observance.
translations.idiomatic: Future Emperor Jianwen’s faction proposed the stone-room compromise.

sentences.zh: 」時陳留范宣兄子問此禮，宣答曰：「舜廟所祭，皆是庶人，其後世遠而毀，不居舜上，不序昭穆。

translations.literal: ” At the time Fan Xuan of Chenliu, his nephew asked this rite; Xuan replied: “What Shun’s temple sacrifices are all commoners; later generations distant then destroyed, not dwelling above Shun, not ordering bright and somber.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xuan compared to Shun’s humble forebears.

sentences.zh: 今四君號猶依本，非以功德致祀也。

translations.literal: Now the four lords’ titles still follow their originals—not merit-based elevation to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They were lords, not cult emperors.

sentences.zh: 若依虞主之瘞，則猶藏子孫之所；

translations.literal: If following Yu’s burying of main tablet, then still burying in descendants’ precinct;
translations.idiomatic: Shun-era burial stayed near heirs.

sentences.zh: 若依夏主之埋，則又非本廟之階。

translations.literal: if following Xia’s burying of main tablet, then again not on original temple’s steps.
translations.idiomatic: Xia buried elsewhere than main stairs.

sentences.zh: 宜思其變，則築一室，親未盡則禘祫處宣帝之上，親盡則無緣下就子孫之列。

translations.literal: It is fitting to ponder the change—then build one chamber: while kin affection has not ended, at di and yin place them above Emperor Xuan; when affection ends they have no reason to descend among grandsons’ rows.
translations.idiomatic: Fan proposed a transitional hall above Xuan.

sentences.zh: 」其後太常劉遐等同蔡謨議。

translations.literal: ” Afterward Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Xia and others joined Cai Mo’s proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Officials coalesced on Cai’s east-facing rite.

sentences.zh: 博士張憑議：「或疑陳于太祖者，皆其後之毀主，憑案古義無別前後之文也。

translations.literal: Erudite Zhang Ping proposed: “Some doubt that arraying before dynastic founder means all later destroyed tablets—Ping examines ancient meaning—there is no text distinguishing earlier and later.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang dismissed order worries among removed tablets.

sentences.zh: 禹不先鯀，則遷主居太祖之上，亦何疑也。

translations.literal: Yu did not rank before Gun—then moved tablet dwelling above dynastic founder—what doubt remains?
translations.idiomatic: Yu above Gun justified odd vertical order.

sentences.zh: 」於是京兆遷入西儲，同謂之祧，如前三祖遷主之禮，故正室猶十一也。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Jingzhao entered western storage, together called distant shrine, like the former three ancestors’ moved-lord rite—hence main chambers still numbered eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao joined the western distant-shrine storage; eleven main bays remained.

sentences.zh: 穆帝崩而哀帝、海西並為兄弟，無所登除。

translations.literal: When Mudi died, Aidi and Haixi were both brothers—nothing ascended or removed.
translations.idiomatic: Brother successions skipped a removal round.

sentences.zh: 咸安之初，簡文皇帝上繼元皇，世秩登進，於是潁川、京兆二主復還昭穆之位。

translations.literal: Early in Xian’an, Emperor Jianwen continued Emperor Yuan, generational rank advanced—thereupon Yingchuan and Jingzhao two masters returned to bright and somber positions.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu’s line restored two tablets.

sentences.zh: 至簡文崩，潁川又遷。

translations.literal: When Jianwen died, Yingchuan again moved.
translations.idiomatic: Another cycle removed Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝太元十二年五月壬戌，詔曰：「昔建太廟，每事從儉，太祖虛位，明堂未建。

translations.literal: Xiaowudi, Taiyuan 12 fifth month renxu, edict said: “Formerly building grand temple, each affair followed frugality—dynastic founder’s seat empty, Bright Hall not yet built.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan 12 reopened capital cult reform.

sentences.zh: 郊祀國之大事，而稽古之制闕然，便可詳議。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice is the state’s great affair, yet examining antiquity’s system is lacking—now may deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for round-mound and Bright Hall plans.

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎中徐邈議：「圓丘郊祀，經典無二，宣皇帝嘗辯斯義，而檢以聖典。

translations.literal: ” Sacrifices section director Xu Miao proposed: “Round mound suburban sacrifice, classics are not dual—Emperor Xuan once debated this meaning, checking against sage canon.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao cited Sima Yi’s precedent on one heaven altar.

sentences.zh: 爰及中興，備加研極，以定南北二郊，誠非異學所可輕改也。

translations.literal: Down to restoration, fully plumb extremes, thereby fixing south and north two suburbs—truly not a heterodox school may lightly alter.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin’s twin suburbs should stand.

sentences.zh: 謂仍舊為安。

translations.literal: We say keeping the old is secure.
translations.idiomatic: Leave suburban layout alone.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝建廟六世，祖三昭三穆。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor built temple for six generations—three bright three somber.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan’s six niches.

sentences.zh: 宣皇帝創基之主，實惟太祖，親則王考。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan is the founder who laid base—truly the dynastic founder—by affection he is royal father.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi was both founder and grandfather line.

sentences.zh: 四廟在上，未及遷世，故權虛東向之位也。

translations.literal: Four temples above, not yet reaching removal generations—hence provisionally empty the east-facing position.
translations.idiomatic: Founder’s seat stayed blank while four generations filled in.

sentences.zh: 兄弟相及，義非二世。

translations.literal: Brothers succeeding one another, in meaning is not two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Brother emperors collapsed generational count.

sentences.zh: 故當今廟祀，世數未足，而欲太祖正位，則違事七之義矣。

translations.literal: Hence today’s temple sacrifice, generation count not yet sufficient, yet desiring dynastic founder’s correct position—then violates serving seven’s meaning.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot crown Xuan while only five lines show.

sentences.zh: 又《禮》曰庶子王亦禘祖立廟，蓋謂支胤援立，則親近必復。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rites says when a bastard-line king also performs di to ancestor and builds temple, it means when a side heir is raised, close lines must return.
translations.idiomatic: Canon allows lateral heirs to reset tablets.

sentences.zh: 京兆府君於今六世，宜復立此室，則宣皇未在六世之上，須前世既遷，乃太祖位定耳。

translations.literal: Jingzhao lord is now six generations—fitting again to erect this chamber—then Emperor Xuan is not yet above six generations; must wait until prior generations have moved—only then is dynastic founder’s position fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao’s fix: restore Jingzhao bay, defer Xuan’s supremacy until removals catch up.

sentences.zh: 京兆遷毀宜藏主於石室，雖禘祫猶弗及。

translations.literal: Jingzhao’s removal and destruction—it is fitting to hide tablets in a stone chamber—even at di and yin they still do not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao said retired Jingzhao tablets should live in a crypt, excluded even from great colligations.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: For what reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why should that be?

sentences.zh: 傳稱毀主升合乎太祖，升者自下之名，不謂可降尊就卑也。

translations.literal: Tradition says destroyed tablets ascend to join the dynastic founder—“ascend” names motion from below—it does not mean one may lower honor to humble rank.
translations.idiomatic: “Ascend” implies promotion, not demoting an ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太子太孫，陰室四主，儲嗣之重，升祔皇祖，所配之廟，世遠應遷，然後從食之孫，與之俱毀。

translations.literal: Crown prince and eldest grandson, four masters in the yin chamber—weight of heir succession—ascending to join imperial grandfather; the temple they pair with, generations distant, ought to move—then grandsons who shared food with them are destroyed together.
translations.idiomatic: Child heirs and their paired shrines rise and fall as one when niches rotate.

sentences.zh: 明堂方圓之制，綱領已舉，不宜闕配帝之祀。

translations.literal: Bright Hall’s square-round design—outline already raised—it is not fitting to omit cult of the god who is paired.
translations.idiomatic: He urged finishing Bright Hall and its high-god pairing.

sentences.zh: 且王者以天下為家，未必一邦，故周平、光武無廢於二京也。

translations.literal: Moreover kings take all under heaven as home—not necessarily one state—hence Zhou Ping and Guangwu were not faulted for two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Dual capitals did not fault Eastern Zhou or Eastern Han.

sentences.zh: 明堂所配之神，積疑莫辯。

translations.literal: The spirit Bright Hall pairs with—accumulated doubts unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Which deity shared Bright Hall remained disputed.

sentences.zh: 案《易》'殷薦上帝，以配祖考'，祖考同配，則上帝亦為天，而嚴父之義顯。

translations.literal: Examining the Changes “Yin offering to the Supreme Lord, pairing ancestors and fathers”—ancestors and fathers paired together—then the Supreme Lord is also Heaven, and the meaning of honoring father as supreme appears.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes merges high god with royal fathers.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》旅上帝者，有故告天，與郊祀常禮同用四圭，故並言之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou’s “marshal the Supreme Lord” means occasional report to heaven—same as suburban sacrifice’s constant rite—using the four-pointed jade—hence spoken together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lumps special and routine heaven reports because both use the same jade.

sentences.zh: 若上帝是五帝，《經》文何不言祀天旅五帝，祀地旅四望乎？

translations.literal: If the Supreme Lord were the Five Emperors, why does scripture not say “sacrifice to heaven and marshal the Five Emperors, sacrifice to earth and marshal the four wang”?
translations.idiomatic: If high god were only the five directional lords, the wording would differ.

sentences.zh: 」侍中車胤議同。

translations.literal: ” Attendant-in-ordinary Che Yin’s opinion agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin concurred.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「明堂之制，既其難詳，且樂主於和，禮主於敬，故質文不同，音器亦殊。

translations.literal: He also said: “Bright Hall’s form, already hard to detail—moreover music roots in harmony, rite roots in reverence—hence plainness and ornament differ, tones and instruments differ.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded flexibility on Bright Hall architecture.

sentences.zh: 既茅茨廣夏，不一其度，何必守其形範，而不弘本從俗乎？

translations.literal: Since thatch huts and broad halls do not share one measure, why cling to outward mold and not enlarge the root and follow custom?
translations.idiomatic: Form should follow function and the age.

sentences.zh: 九服咸寧，河朔無塵，然後明堂辟雍可崇而修之。

translations.literal: When the nine domains are all calm and Hebei free of dust, then Bright Hall and circular moat may be exalted and built.
translations.idiomatic: Defer monumental works until the north is reconquered.

sentences.zh: 」時朝議多同，於是奉行，一無所改。

translations.literal: ” At the time court debate mostly agreed—thereupon they carried it out, changing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The court tabled major reform.

sentences.zh: 十六年，始改作太廟殿，正室十四間，東西儲各一間，合十六間，棟高八丈四尺。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, first rebuilt grand temple hall—fourteen main chambers, one east and one west storage—sixteen total—ridge height eight zhang four chi.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan 16 expanded the hall to sixteen bays.

sentences.zh: 備法駕遷神主於行廟，征西至京兆四主及太子太孫各用其位之儀服。

translations.literal: With full imperial equipage they moved spirit tablets to the traveling temple—General Who Conquers the West through Jingzhao four masters and crown prince and eldest grandson each used regalia matching their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Procession matched Taikang except for four lords’ reduced pomp.

sentences.zh: 四主不從帝者之儀，是與太康異也。

translations.literal: The four masters did not follow imperial ceremony—this differs from Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin had given those tablets full imperial escort; Jin did not.

sentences.zh: 諸主既入廟，設脯醢之奠。

translations.literal: When all masters entered temple, they set dried meat and pickle oblations.
translations.idiomatic: Interim offerings marked installation.

sentences.zh: 及新廟成，神主還室，又設脯醢之奠。

translations.literal: When new temple was completed, spirit tablets returned to chambers, again they set dried meat and pickle oblations.
translations.idiomatic: Second offering marked final seating.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，追尊簡文母會稽太妃鄭氏為簡文皇帝宣太后，立廟太廟道西。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year second month, posthumously honored Jianwen’s mother Grand Concubine Zheng of Kuaiji as Empress Xuan of Emperor Jianwen, establishing temple west of grand temple approach.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu’s mother received a chapel beside the main line.

sentences.zh: 及孝武崩，京兆又遷，如穆帝之世四祧故事。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died, Jingzhao again moved, following Mudi-era story of four distant shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Another emperor’s death cycled Jingzhao into western storage like before.

sentences.zh: 義熙九年四月，將殷祠，詔博議遷毀之禮。

translations.literal: Yixi 9 fourth month, about to hold yin sacrifice, edict ordered broad debate on removal and destruction rite.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu’s court reopened the tablet-storage fight.

sentences.zh: 大司馬琅邪王德文議：「泰始之初，虛太祖之位，而緣情流遠，上及征西，故世盡則宜毀，而宣帝正太祖之位。

translations.literal: Grand marshal Prince of Langye Sima Dewen proposed: “Taishi’s opening left dynastic founder’s seat empty, yet affection flowed far up to General Who Conquers the West—hence when generations end they ought be destroyed and Emperor Xuan takes correct founder position.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen argued four lords should leave the active line.

sentences.zh: 又漢光武移十一帝主於洛邑，則毀主不設，理可推矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Han Guangwu moved eleven emperors’ tablets to Luoyang—then destroyed tablets were not set up—principle may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han buried old tablets without niches.

sentences.zh: 宜築別室，以居四府君之主，永藏而弗祀也。

translations.literal: It is fitting to build separate chambers to house the four lords’ masters, eternally storing without sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Seal them in a side hall and stop feeding them.

sentences.zh: 」大司農徐廣議：「四府君嘗處廟堂之首，歆率土之祭，若埋之幽壤，於情理未必咸盡。

translations.literal: ” Minister of Finance Xu Guang proposed: “The four lords once stood at temple’s head, enjoying all-soil sacrifice—if buried in dark earth, sentiment and principle may not both be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang resisted outright burial.

sentences.zh: 謂可遷藏西儲，以為遠祧，而禘饗永絕也。

translations.literal: We say they may be moved to western storage, taken as distant shrine, while di feasting ends forever.
translations.idiomatic: Western annex as remote shrine without di inclusion.

sentences.zh: 」太尉諮議參軍袁豹議：「仍舊無革，殷祠猶及四府君，情理為允。

translations.literal: ” Army consultant Yuan Bao proposed: “Keeping the old without reform—yin sacrifice still reaches four lords—sentiment and principle are balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wanted status quo until reform.

sentences.zh: 」時劉裕作輔，意與大司馬議同，須後殷祠行事改制。

translations.literal: ” At the time Liu Yu assisted governance, his intent matched the grand marshal—waiting until after yin sacrifice to change system.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sided with Dewen but delayed action.

sentences.zh: 會安帝崩，未及禘而天祿終焉。

translations.literal: Then Andi died—before di could occur the mandate ended.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell before the rite was settled.

sentences.zh: 武帝咸寧五年十一月己酉，弘訓羊太后崩，宗廟廢一時之祀，天地明堂去樂，且不上胙。

translations.literal: Wudi, Xianning 5 eleventh month jiyou, Empress Dowager Hongxun Lady Yang died—ancestral temple suspended one season’s sacrifice—heaven, earth, and Bright Hall removed music, and did not distribute sacrificial meat.
translations.idiomatic: National mourning silenced high cults and banquets.

sentences.zh: 穆帝升平五年十月己卯，殷祀，以帝崩後不作樂。

translations.literal: Mudi, Shengping 5 tenth month jimao, yin sacrifice—because after the emperor’s death they made no music.
translations.idiomatic: Court skipped music at yin after a death.

sentences.zh: 孝武太元十一年九月，皇女亡，及應烝祠，中書侍郎范寧奏：「案《喪服傳》有死宮中者三月不舉祭，不別長幼之與貴賤也。

translations.literal: Xiaowu, Taiyuan 11 ninth month, imperial daughter died—when autumn steam sacrifice fell due, palace secretary Fan Ning memorialized: “Examining Mourning Dress commentary, death inside palace halts sacrifice three months—without distinguishing elder or younger, noble or base.
translations.idiomatic: Fan cited three-month suspension after an in-palace death.

sentences.zh: 皇女雖在嬰孩，臣竊以為疑。

translations.literal: Though the imperial daughter was still an infant, your servant privately holds doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned applying the rule to a baby princess.

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書奏使三公行事。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the masters of writing memorialized to have the three excellencies conduct the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers delegated the steam rite to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始七年四月，帝將親祠，車駕夕牲，而儀注還不拜。

translations.literal: Wudi, Taishi 7 fourth month, the emperor was about to sacrifice in person; imperial equipage inspected victims evening before, yet ceremonial commentary on return did not include bow.
translations.idiomatic: Evening victim inspection skipped the bow on exit.

sentences.zh: 詔問其故，博士奏歷代相承如此。

translations.literal: Edict asked the reason; erudites memorialized successive generations were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars pleaded precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非致敬宗廟之禮也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “This is not rite for reverently greeting the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded a respectful bow.

sentences.zh: 」於是實拜而還，遂以為制，夕牲必躬臨拜，而江左以來復止。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he truly bowed on return, then took it as regulation—evening victim inspection must personally attend bow—yet since crossing the river they again stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin made the bow norm; Eastern Jin dropped it again.

sentences.zh: 魏故事，天子為次殿於廟殿之北東，天子入自北門。

translations.literal: Wei precedent: the Son of Heaven made a resting hall north-east of temple hall—Son of Heaven entered from north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei kept a north-side robing room.

sentences.zh: 新禮，設次殿于南門中門外之右，天子入自南門。

translations.literal: New ritual set resting hall outside south gate’s middle gate on the right—Son of Heaven entered from south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jin reform opened a southern approach.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「次殿所以為解息之處，凡適尊以不顯為恭，以由隱為順，而設之於上位，入自南門，非謙厭之義。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: “Resting hall is where one unties and rests—in all approaching the honored, not exposing is reverent, passing hidden is compliant—yet setting it in the upper position, entering from south gate—is not meaning of humble avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu called the southern layout immodest.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮，皆如舊說。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix new ritual entirely like old explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Revert to Wei’s north entry.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” They followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Court agreed.

sentences.zh: 禮，大事則告祖禰，小事則特告禰，秦漢久廢。

translations.literal: Rite: great affairs then announce to dynastic founder and father; small affairs then announce only to father—Qin and Han long abandoned this.
translations.idiomatic: Classical report rites lapsed in empire.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年七月，將東巡，以大軍當出，使太常以特牛告南郊。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi, Huangchu 4 seventh month, about to tour east because great army would march, ordered chamberlain to announce with special ox at southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Same campaign notice to heaven as before.

sentences.zh: 及文帝崩，又使太尉告諡策於南郊。

translations.literal: When Wendi died, again ordered grand commandant to announce posthumous patent at southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Death also reported south of the city.

sentences.zh: 自是迄晉相承，告郊之後仍以告廟，至江左其禮廢。

translations.literal: From this through Jin succession continued—after announcing suburb they still announced temple—south of the river the rite lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin dropped temple announcement after suburb.

sentences.zh: 至成帝咸和三年，蘇峻覆亂京都，溫嶠等立行廟于白石，復行其典。

translations.literal: By Chengdi, Xianhe 3, Su Jun overturned the capital—Wen Jiao and others set traveling temple at Baishi, again performing the canon.
translations.idiomatic: Exile court revived report rites at a field shrine.

sentences.zh: 告先君及後曰：「逆臣蘇峻，傾覆社稷，毀棄三正。

translations.literal: Announcing to former lords and later said: “Rebel subject Su Jun overturned soil and grain, destroyed the three legitimacies.
translations.idiomatic: They accused Su of wrecking dynastic order.

sentences.zh: 污辱海內。

translations.literal: He defiled all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: They listed his pollution of the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣侃、臣嶠、臣亮等手刃戎首，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: Your subjects Kan, Jiao, Liang and others personally beheaded the war-chief, executing heaven’s punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Generals claimed credit for crushing the coup.

sentences.zh: 惟中宗元皇帝、肅祖明皇帝、明穆皇后之靈，降鑒有罪，剿絕其命，翦此群凶，以安宗廟。

translations.literal: May spirits of Middle Ancestor Emperor Yuan, Revered Ancestor Emperor Ming, and Bright and Grave Empress look down on the guilty, cut off their fate, exterminate this pack of villains, to pacify the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer invoked recent emperors to bless the loyalists.

sentences.zh: 臣等雖隕首摧軀，猶生之年。」

translations.literal: Though your subjects lose heads and break bodies, it is still within our living years.”
translations.idiomatic: They pledged total sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和三年，詔曰：「禮，王后無嗣，擇建支子，以繼大宗，則當纂正統而奉公義，何得復顧私親哉！

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi, Taihe 3, edict said: “Rite: when the queen lacks heir, choose and establish a collateral son to continue the great line—then one ought inherit correct line and uphold public duty—how may one again heed private kin!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui warned lateral heirs against ennobling birth parents.

sentences.zh: 漢宣繼昭帝后，加悼考以皇號。

translations.literal: Han Xuandi, succeeding Emperor Zhao, added posthumous title “Mourned Father” with imperial style.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun’s case showed the temptation.

sentences.zh: 哀帝以外籓援立，而董宏等稱引亡秦，惑誤朝議，遂尊恭皇，立廟京師。

translations.literal: Aidi, raised from outer fief, yet Dong Hong and others cited dead Qin, misleading court debate—thereupon they honored Respectful King, building temple in capital.
translations.idiomatic: Han Aidi’s fathers’ cult veered into impropriety.

sentences.zh: 又寵籓妾，使比長信，僭差無禮，人神弗佑。

translations.literal: They also favored a concubine-mother, comparing her to Dowager Changxin—usurpation and disorder without rite—men and spirits did not bless.
translations.idiomatic: Petty consorts gained empress parity.

sentences.zh: 非罪師丹忠正之諫，用致丁傅焚如之禍。

translations.literal: Had it not been for Shi Dan’s loyal remonstrance, they would have brought Ding and Fu’s fire-brand calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Good ministers averted a worse flame.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，相踵行之。

translations.literal: From this onward they trod the path one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han kept repeating the mistake.

sentences.zh: 其令公卿有司，深以前世為戒。

translations.literal: Order dukes and offices deeply take former ages as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui commanded memory of Han errors.

sentences.zh: 後嗣萬一有由諸侯入奉大統，則當明為人後之義。

translations.literal: If later heirs happen to enter the great line from a marquisate, then clarify the meaning of becoming another’s heir.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted heirs must obey main-line duty.

sentences.zh: 敢為佞邪導諛君上，妄建非正之號，謂考為皇，稱妣為後，則股肱大臣誅之無赦。

translations.literal: Whoever dares flatter with heterodox paths, misleading the sovereign, rashly establishing illegitimate titles, calling father “emperor,” mother “empress”—then pillar ministers shall execute them without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Death for those who ennoble private parents.

sentences.zh: 其書之金策，藏之宗廟。

translations.literal: Inscribe it on metal book, store in ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The oath was metal-bound and archived.

sentences.zh: 」是後高貴、常道援立，皆不外尊。

translations.literal: ” After this, Gaogui and Changdao’s elevations did not honor outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei child emperors skipped private parent cults.

sentences.zh: 及湣帝建興四年，司徒梁芬議追尊之禮，帝既不從，而左僕射索綝等亦稱引魏制，以為不可，故追贈吳王為太保而已。

translations.literal: When Mindi, Jianxing 4, Minister of Education Liang Fen debated posthumous honor rite, the emperor did not follow; yet vice director Suo Lin and others also cited Wei regulations as impermissible—hence posthumous gift to Prince of Wu stopped at grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin’s last emperor could not title his father emperor.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興二年，有司言琅邪恭王宜稱皇考。

translations.literal: Yuandi, Taixing 2, offices said Prince Gong of Langye ought be called “Imperial Father.”
translations.idiomatic: Some wanted Sima Rui’s father elevated.

sentences.zh: 賀循議云：「禮典之義，子不敢以己爵加其父號。

translations.literal: He Xun argued: “Canon meaning—a son dares not add his own noble rank to his father’s title.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun blocked “emperor father” for the late prince.

sentences.zh: 」帝又從之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui accepted restraint.
